Exam Details

The Florida Residential Plumbing Inspector examination is identified as ICC 1P within the International Code Council's Florida examination program.

The examination evaluates technical knowledge associated with inspecting plumbing systems installed in residential buildings.

  • Examination: Residential Plumbing Inspector.
  • Florida Exam ID: ICC 1P.
  • Examination Organization: International Code Council (ICC).
  • Examination Type: Technical certification examination.
  • Number of Questions: 60 multiple-choice questions.
  • Time Limit: 2 hours.
  • Examination Format: Open book.
  • Examination Code Cycle: 2021 International Residential Code.
  • Primary Reference: 2021 International Residential Code for One- and Two-Family Dwellings.
  • Testing Method: ICC PRONTO remote-proctored testing for Florida DBPR candidates.
  • Florida Licensing Authority: Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation and the Building Code Administrators and Inspectors Board.

The ICC 1P examination covers six principal content areas: General Requirements, Fixtures, Water Heaters, Water Supply and Distribution, Sanitary Drainage, and Vents.

These categories reflect the technical responsibilities involved in inspecting residential plumbing installations and identifying conditions that do not comply with applicable code provisions.

Open Book Test

The Florida Residential Plumbing Inspector (ICC 1P) examination is an open book test. Candidates may use reference materials permitted under the applicable ICC examination policies.

Although the examination allows reference use, successful preparation requires more than knowing how to search a code book.

Candidates must recognize the plumbing system described in a question, identify the applicable requirements, interpret technical provisions, and apply them to residential construction conditions.

With 60 questions and a two-hour time limit, candidates have an average of approximately two minutes per question.

Efficient reference navigation is therefore an important preparation skill.

For example, a question involving drainage pipe slope requires a different section from one concerning fixture clearances, water heater protection, or water distribution sizing.

Practice using the International Residential Code's table of contents, index, definitions, plumbing chapters, and technical tables.

Become familiar with the organization of the code before completing timed practice questions.

Reference materials must comply with ICC rules for the selected testing method. AI tutoring platforms and general online study resources are intended for examination preparation rather than use during a proctored test.

ACE encourages candidates to develop stronger code-navigation habits through targeted review and technical explanations.

  2. Evaluate professional qualifications: Review the applicable construction experience, inspection experience, education, and professional qualification pathways.

  4. Apply through Florida DBPR: Complete the appropriate Building Code Administrators and Inspectors Board application.
  5. Study the technical examination: Review the ICC 1P content outline and designated residential plumbing reference.
  6. Prepare for Florida Principles and Practice: Study Florida construction laws and professional regulations when required.
  7. Complete the examinations: Follow the applicable examination authorization and testing procedures.
  8. Finish certification requirements: Submit remaining documentation and satisfy the applicable state licensing conditions.

Florida identifies the BCAIB 1 application for initial inspector certification by examination.

Examination preparation and professional licensing are separate responsibilities. The ACE free demo provides educational study support rather than examination registration or application services.

Florida State Requirements

Florida regulates building code inspectors through Chapter 468, Part XII, Florida Statutes, and the Building Code Administrators and Inspectors Board.

Residential inspection work is regulated under Florida's professional certification framework. Individuals performing regulated inspection duties must hold the appropriate certification or other lawful authorization.

Applicants must be at least 18 years old, demonstrate good moral character, and satisfy an approved professional qualification pathway.

Florida recognizes qualifying construction experience, relevant education, inspection experience, and other professional qualifications established under state law.

For the applicable Residential Inspector experience pathway, Florida has removed the requirement to demonstrate supervisory operational control and direction. Relevant construction-related, hands-on, or related-field experience remains necessary.

Initial inspector certification by examination generally requires passing an ICC technical examination and the Florida Principles and Practice examination.

Existing qualifying Florida building code professionals who maintain the required continuous licensure may not need to repeat the Principles and Practice examination when pursuing an additional certification.

Florida inspectors enforce the legally applicable Florida Building Code and associated regulations. The ICC 1P examination uses the 2021 International Residential Code designated for its technical examination content.

Understanding the distinction between examination references and Florida's adopted construction requirements helps candidates prepare for both testing and professional responsibilities.

Reference Books

The Florida ICC 1P Residential Plumbing Inspector examination identifies the following primary technical reference.

  • 2021 International Residential Code for One- and Two-Family Dwellings (IRC)
    Provides residential plumbing requirements involving fixtures, water heaters, water supply and distribution, sanitary drainage, vents, approved piping materials, installation methods, testing, and piping protection. The code also addresses other residential construction provisions relevant to plumbing inspections.

The International Residential Code organizes plumbing requirements into subject-specific chapters and provisions.

Its plumbing sections contain important installation conditions, sizing tables, material requirements, and safety provisions used to evaluate residential plumbing work.

Learning the organization of this reference supports more efficient examination preparation and stronger understanding of residential plumbing standards.

Test Information and Study Materials

The Florida ICC 1P Residential Plumbing Inspector examination evaluates six major content categories. Understanding their relative importance can help candidates organize a balanced study plan.

General Requirements – 14%: Review permit requirements, inspections, approved materials, piping protection, installation methods, testing, and general plumbing provisions.

Candidates should understand how plumbing systems are evaluated for appropriate materials, supports, connections, and protection from damage.

Fixtures – 8%: Study plumbing fixture requirements, approved fixtures, installation conditions, connections, clearances, and related residential plumbing provisions.

Preparation includes familiarity with toilets, sinks, bathtubs, showers, and other common residential fixtures.

Water Heaters – 11%: Review water heater installation, temperature and pressure relief protection, equipment connections, discharge piping, and installation safety requirements.

Water Supply and Distribution – 22%: Study potable water systems, water service piping, distribution materials, pipe sizing, pressure requirements, valves, and backflow prevention.

Sanitary Drainage – 23%: Review drainage piping, fixture drains, branches, building drains, slopes, sizing, cleanouts, fittings, and installation requirements.

Vents – 22%: Study plumbing vent systems, vent sizing, connections, venting methods, termination requirements, and protection of fixture trap seals.

Sanitary Drainage is the largest individual examination category, accounting for 23% of the content outline.

Water Supply and Distribution and Vents each represent 22%.

Together, these three categories account for 67% of the examination, making them particularly important subjects for technical preparation.

Preparing for Sanitary Drainage Questions

Sanitary drainage is a major responsibility of residential plumbing inspectors.

Drainage systems must convey wastewater through properly installed piping while maintaining the required flow conditions.

Study drainage fixture units, pipe sizing, slope, cleanouts, and drainage connections.

Review the differences between fixture drains, branch drains, stacks, building drains, and building sewers.

Practice identifying the fittings and installation arrangements described in technical questions.

Develop familiarity with how the International Residential Code addresses changes in direction, drainage pipe materials, and required access for cleaning.

When reviewing practice questions, identify the drainage component involved before locating the applicable technical requirement.

Understanding complete drainage systems helps candidates recognize how separate components work together in residential plumbing installations.

Understanding Water Supply and Distribution

Residential water supply systems must deliver potable water to plumbing fixtures and connected equipment.

Inspectors evaluate water service connections, distribution piping, approved materials, pressure conditions, and protection against contamination.

Study the relationship between plumbing fixture demand and pipe sizing.

Review approved piping materials, joints, fittings, valves, supports, and installation methods.

Develop familiarity with backflow prevention requirements and the importance of protecting potable water supplies.

Practice interpreting technical tables involving water distribution and piping systems.

Some examination questions involve multiple conditions, making careful reading and understanding of code terminology especially important.

ACE encourages candidates to strengthen these skills through technical explanations and practice-oriented review.

Venting Systems and Trap Protection

Plumbing vent systems are essential components of residential sanitary drainage.

Vents help maintain appropriate pressure conditions within drainage systems and protect plumbing fixture trap seals.

Study vent connections, vent sizing, permitted venting arrangements, and termination requirements.

Review how vent piping interacts with fixture drains, branch drains, and drainage stacks.

Become familiar with the different venting methods addressed by the International Residential Code.

Practice recognizing how the location of fixtures and drainage connections influences applicable venting requirements.

Understand why improper vent arrangements can interfere with drainage performance and trap protection.

Developing a clear understanding of vent systems helps connect installation knowledge with inspection responsibilities.

Water Heater Installation and Safety Requirements

Water heaters are another important subject for residential plumbing inspection.

Study equipment installation requirements, accessibility, clearances, and proper plumbing connections.

Review temperature and pressure relief valves and their associated discharge piping provisions.

Understand how water heater location and equipment type affect applicable installation requirements.

Practice identifying common conditions that require inspection attention.

For fuel-burning equipment, become familiar with the relationship between water heater operation and applicable combustion air and venting provisions.

Water heater questions often connect several technical requirements, making organized reference study especially useful.

Plumbing Fixtures and General Inspection Requirements

Residential plumbing inspection also involves evaluating the installation of fixtures and the general requirements applying to plumbing systems.

Review fixture connections, installation clearances, approved materials, and proper support.

Study how plumbing piping must be protected against corrosion, freezing, physical damage, and other harmful conditions.

Become familiar with the requirements for piping penetrations and the protection of structural building components.

Review plumbing system testing and the responsibilities involved in identifying installation deficiencies.

Practice connecting the requirements established in the code with the conditions encountered during residential construction inspections.

These foundational topics reinforce understanding across all six examination categories.

Building Stronger Code Navigation Skills

Efficient code navigation can make examination preparation more productive.

Begin by learning how the International Residential Code organizes plumbing systems.

Use the index to identify key terms and review the corresponding technical provisions.

Become familiar with the locations of common tables involving drainage, venting, and water distribution.

Practice distinguishing between general provisions and requirements applying to specific installations.

For every practice question, identify the subject, locate the relevant provision, and review the reasoning behind the answer.

Consistent code-navigation practice can strengthen technical knowledge and help candidates manage their time during an open book examination.

Exam Details

The Florida Certified Plumbing Contractor examination is administered through the Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation (DBPR) under the Construction Industry Licensing Board.

Plumbing contractor candidates must complete the required General Trade Knowledge and Business and Finance examinations.

  • License Classification: Florida Certified Plumbing Contractor.
  • Licensing Authority: Florida DBPR and Construction Industry Licensing Board.
  • Trade Examination: Plumbing Contractors General Trade Knowledge.
  • Trade Examination: 110 multiple-choice questions and five isometric drawings.
  • Morning Session: 45 multiple-choice questions and five isometric drawings.
  • Afternoon Session: 65 multiple-choice questions.
  • Session Duration: 4 hours and 30 minutes per session.
  • Trade Testing Method: Paper-and-pencil examination.
  • Additional Examination: Business and Finance.
  • Business and Finance: 120 scored questions with a 6-hour-and-30-minute time limit.
  • Examination Format: Open book.
  • Examination Registration: Professional Testing, Inc.
  • Business and Finance Testing Provider: Pearson VUE.

The plumbing trade examination is administered on scheduled dates rather than through the daily computer-based testing system used for many other Florida contractor trades.

The examination evaluates plumbing systems, technical calculations, construction standards, installation methods, and trade-specific drawings.

Open Book Test

The Florida Plumbing Contractor examination is an open book test. Candidates may bring the reference materials authorized by Florida DBPR for the applicable examination.

Open book testing requires effective preparation because plumbing questions involve calculations, code interpretation, equipment requirements, and practical field knowledge.

Florida permits highlighting and underlining in approved references. Handwritten or typewritten notes are prohibited, and removable tabs are not allowed.

References must remain properly bound. Candidates may bring only one copy of each approved reference, and no additional markings may be made during testing.

For the plumbing trade examination, candidates must also bring a small 30/60-degree triangle for completing isometric drawings.

Isometric drawing preparation is especially important because candidates must demonstrate the ability to represent plumbing piping arrangements clearly.

ACE encourages candidates to practice locating information in plumbing codes, interpreting technical tables, and understanding how installation requirements apply to actual projects.

Digital AI tutoring tools are intended for examination preparation rather than use during the proctored examination.

Licensing Steps

Becoming a Florida Certified Plumbing Contractor involves meeting professional qualifications, completing required examinations, and obtaining state certification.

  1. Understand the license: Review the authorized scope of plumbing contracting under Florida law.
  2. Evaluate your qualifications: Review your plumbing experience, supervisory responsibilities, and applicable education.
  3. Study the examinations: Prepare for Plumbing General Trade Knowledge and Business and Finance.
  4. Obtain approved references: Study the applicable Florida Building Code volumes, plumbing manuals, and safety publications.
  5. Practice isometric drawings: Develop the skills needed to interpret and draw plumbing piping systems.
  6. Register for testing: Apply through Professional Testing, Inc. and complete the examination scheduling process.
  7. Complete the examinations: Take the scheduled plumbing trade examination and the separate Business and Finance examination.
  8. Apply for certification: Submit the appropriate Florida DBPR Certified Plumbing Contractor application.
  9. Complete licensing requirements: Provide the required experience documentation and satisfy applicable financial responsibility, insurance, and background screening conditions.

Passing the examinations is an important stage in the licensing process. Florida certification also requires approval of the applicable contractor application.

State Requirements

Florida regulates plumbing contractors under Chapter 489, Part I, Florida Statutes, through the Construction Industry Licensing Board.

A Florida Certified Plumbing Contractor has broad authority within the plumbing trade, subject to applicable laws and licensing restrictions.

The classification includes authorized work involving water supply, sanitary drainage, storm drainage, venting systems, sewer systems, irrigation, swimming pool piping, and related plumbing equipment.

The authorized scope also includes specified natural gas and liquefied petroleum gas piping, medical gas systems, solar water heating systems, and other specialized piping applications.

Applicants for initial certification must satisfy an approved experience and education qualification pathway.

Florida recognizes combinations of qualifying field experience, foreman experience, construction-related education, and other approved credentials.

One qualification pathway involves four years of qualifying experience as a worker or foreman, including at least one year as a foreman.

Applicants must also meet the applicable financial responsibility, examination, insurance, and professional licensing requirements.

Understanding the legal scope of a Plumbing Contractor license helps candidates connect technical examination preparation with their responsibilities as licensed construction professionals.

Reference Books

The following publications are identified on the Florida Plumbing Contractor Trade Knowledge reference list for January through December 2026.

  • Chapter 64E-6, Florida Administrative Code, Standards for Onsite Sewage Treatment and Disposal Systems, July 16, 2018
    Addresses onsite sewage treatment and disposal systems, including regulatory provisions relevant to septic system work. A properly bound PDF edition is permitted.
  • Code of Federal Regulations, OSHA 29 CFR Part 1926, July 1, 2025
    Provides construction safety requirements covering excavation, personal protective equipment, ladders, scaffolds, equipment, and jobsite hazards.
  • Mathematics for Plumbers and Pipefitters, 8th Edition, 2013
    Provides practical mathematical instruction involving measurements, fractions, dimensions, pipe calculations, and construction-related problem-solving.
  • NFPA 14 – Standard for the Installation of Standpipe and Hose Systems, 2019
    Addresses the installation of standpipe and hose systems used for fire protection within buildings.
  • NFPA 99 – Health Care Facilities Code, 2021
    Provides requirements concerning healthcare facility systems. The designated examination portions include Chapters 3 and 5 and Annexes A and C.
  • Plumber's Handbook Revised, 5th Edition, 2018, or 6th Edition, 2023
    Provides practical plumbing reference information, including piping calculations, materials, technical tables, and installation guidance.
  • Solar Thermal Manual: Solar Water & Pool Heating Manual, 2006
    Explains solar water and pool heating systems, equipment, components, and installation principles. A properly bound PDF edition is permitted.
  • Florida Building Code – Mechanical, 2023 Edition
    Provides mechanical system requirements relevant to equipment installation, ventilation, and associated piping applications.
  • Florida Building Code – Accessibility, 2023 Edition
    Addresses accessibility requirements involving plumbing fixtures, facilities, dimensions, and clearances.
  • Florida Building Code – Plumbing, 2023 Edition
    Provides requirements for plumbing fixtures, sanitary drainage, venting, water distribution, water heaters, and storm drainage systems.
  • Florida Building Code – Residential, 2023 Edition
    Addresses residential plumbing requirements and construction provisions applicable to one- and two-family dwellings and related structures.
  • Florida Building Code – Fuel Gas, 2023 Edition
    Provides requirements for gas piping, appliance connections, combustion air, venting, and fuel gas installation safety.

Test Information and Study Materials

The Plumbing Contractors General Trade Knowledge examination evaluates the knowledge needed to install, maintain, repair, and manage plumbing systems.

Drainage Systems: Review sanitary drainage, storm drainage, waste piping, venting, roof drainage, piping materials, sizing, and installation requirements.

Water Distribution: Study water supply systems, pipe sizing, pressure, fixture demand, valves, backflow prevention, and water service installations.

Natural Gas Piping: Review fuel gas piping materials, system sizing, regulators, appliance connections, and applicable code requirements.

Medical Gas Piping: Study oxygen, vacuum, medical air, and related healthcare piping applications within the authorized plumbing trade.

Industrial Piping: Review specialized piping arrangements, materials, installation considerations, and technical requirements.

Solar Systems: Explore solar water heating principles, piping arrangements, equipment components, and system applications.

Fire Protection: Review standpipe systems, related piping, and applicable fire protection installation requirements.

Plumbing Mathematics: Practice measurements, conversions, pipe calculations, areas, volumes, and construction mathematics.

Isometric Drawings: Develop the ability to interpret plumbing piping arrangements and represent systems through three-dimensional isometric diagrams.

The examination also evaluates plan reading, construction specifications, safety practices, installation methods, maintenance, and the use of plumbing tools and equipment.

Preparing for Plumbing Isometric Drawings

Isometric drawings are a distinctive part of the Florida Plumbing Contractor trade examination.

These drawings represent piping systems using a three-dimensional perspective that helps communicate direction, elevations, and connections.

Begin by reviewing the differences between plan views, elevations, and isometric diagrams.

Practice identifying vertical piping, horizontal branches, fittings, drainage connections, and changes in direction.

Develop familiarity with illustrating plumbing systems using consistent angles and clear connections.

Study the relationship between sanitary drainage, vent piping, and fixture connections.

When practicing, concentrate on accurately representing the piping arrangement rather than simply reproducing a memorized drawing.

Consistent drawing practice complements written examination preparation and reinforces your understanding of how plumbing systems connect.

How to Study Drainage and Venting Systems

Drainage and venting are foundational subjects for plumbing contractors.

Review drainage fixture units, pipe sizing, slopes, cleanouts, fittings, and system connections.

Study how sanitary drainage systems carry wastewater and how venting arrangements protect trap seals.

Become familiar with roof drainage, stormwater piping, and the calculations used to evaluate drainage capacity.

Practice locating important code provisions and tables in the Florida Building Code – Plumbing.

Understanding the relationship between drainage and venting helps candidates approach technical questions involving complete piping systems.

Understanding Water Distribution and Gas Piping

Water distribution and gas piping require careful attention to system design and technical requirements.

For water distribution, study fixture demand, pipe sizing, water pressure, supply materials, valves, and backflow prevention.

Review how building layouts influence piping arrangements and equipment connections.

For fuel gas systems, develop familiarity with approved piping materials, sizing methods, appliance connections, shutoff valves, and regulators.

Practice identifying which technical requirements apply to the system described in an examination question.

These subjects benefit from a combination of calculation practice and reference navigation.

Preparing for Medical Gas and Specialty Plumbing

Florida plumbing contractors may encounter specialized systems beyond conventional residential plumbing.

Medical gas piping requires knowledge of healthcare-related piping systems and applicable technical standards.

Review the purpose of oxygen, vacuum, and other medical gas distribution systems.

Study the distinction between general plumbing work and specialized installations requiring additional technical knowledge.

Other examination subjects include fire protection piping, solar water heating, and industrial piping applications.

Develop familiarity with the relevant reference books and the conditions affecting these installations.

Even experienced residential plumbers benefit from reviewing these specialized trade areas during examination preparation.

  3. Register for the Examinations: Apply for the required construction examinations through Professional Testing, Inc.
  4. Prepare for Both Examinations: Study Plumbing General Trade Knowledge and Business & Finance using appropriate preparation resources.
  5. Schedule Your Examinations: Follow the scheduled paper-and-pencil plumbing examination process and arrange the computer-based Business & Finance examination through Pearson VUE after approval.
  6. Complete the Required Examinations: Pass the examination components applicable to your certification.
  7. Submit Your Licensing Application: Apply to the Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation using the appropriate contractor certification application.
  8. Meet Remaining State Requirements: Complete applicable licensing conditions before performing regulated plumbing contracting work.

Examination approval and contractor licensing approval are separate processes. Passing the required examinations is an important step toward certification but does not independently authorize someone to operate as a licensed Plumbing Contractor.

Florida Plumbing Contractors are regulated under Chapter 489 of the Florida Statutes. The Plumbing Contractor classification belongs to Division II of the state's construction contractor licensing system.

Florida Plumbing Contractor Scope of Work

Florida Plumbing Contractors have broad authority within the plumbing trade, including the installation, maintenance, repair, alteration, and extension of qualifying plumbing systems.

The statutory scope includes numerous activities associated with residential, commercial, and specialized plumbing installations.

  • Sanitary drainage and storm drainage systems.
  • Water distribution and supply systems.
  • Drainage and venting systems.
  • Natural gas and related piping systems.
  • Medical gas piping and related systems.
  • Water and sewer lines.
  • Swimming pool piping and irrigation systems.
  • Solar water-heating systems.
  • Qualifying industrial and process piping.

The classification also includes certain additional piping, equipment, and related activities under Florida law. Contractors must perform authorized work in accordance with applicable codes, regulations, and professional requirements.

Certified vs. Registered Plumbing Contractor

Florida distinguishes between certified and registered contractors.

A state-certified Plumbing Contractor may perform authorized plumbing contracting activities throughout Florida, subject to applicable laws, permitting requirements, and local regulations.

A registered Plumbing Contractor's authority is associated with the local jurisdiction or jurisdictions for which the registration is valid.

This distinction is important when selecting a licensing pathway and planning future business activities.

Experience and Education Requirements

Florida Plumbing Contractor applicants must establish qualifying experience or an accepted combination of education and experience under applicable state licensing rules.

Relevant experience may include plumbing installation, drainage systems, water distribution, piping work, or qualifying supervisory responsibilities.

Applicants must provide the documentation required by their licensing application.

Financial Responsibility and Insurance

Florida Plumbing Contractor applicants must satisfy applicable financial responsibility, insurance, and other licensing requirements.

These obligations are separate from the knowledge evaluated during the Business & Finance examination and represent important responsibilities of professional contracting.

Test Information and Study Materials

Plumbing Trade Knowledge Study Topics

The Florida Plumbing General Trade Knowledge examination covers several major technical content areas.

  • Drainage (20%): Review sanitary drainage, drainage components, venting relationships, and plumbing system principles.
  • Water Distribution (20%): Study water supply systems, distribution piping, pressure considerations, and installation principles.
  • Natural Gas Piping (15%): Review gas piping components, distribution concepts, sizing principles, and applicable safety considerations.
  • Medical Gas Piping (20%): Understand piping systems associated with medical gases and related installation requirements.
  • Industrial Piping (10%): Review specialized piping systems and industrial piping applications.
  • Swimming Pools, Wells, and Irrigation (5%): Study piping principles associated with water wells, pools, and irrigation systems.
  • Solar (5%): Review plumbing applications involving solar water-heating systems.
  • Fire Protection (5%): Reinforce knowledge of piping applications associated with qualifying fire protection systems.

These content areas provide a foundation for organizing technical plumbing study sessions.

Plumbing Isometric Drawing Preparation

One distinguishing feature of the Florida Plumbing Contractor trade examination is its isometric drawing component.

Candidates must prepare five plumbing isometric drawings demonstrating their understanding of plumbing system layouts and piping relationships.

Important drawing principles include:

  • Accurate representation of plumbing fixtures and piping.
  • Proper orientation of system components.
  • Clear identification of drainage and venting relationships.
  • Correct representation of piping connections.
  • Appropriate isometric drawing angles.
  • Clear labeling and legible presentation.

Flash cards can reinforce terminology and system knowledge, but successful drawing preparation also requires hands-on practice creating and interpreting plumbing isometric drawings.

Business & Finance Study Topics

The Florida Construction Business & Finance examination evaluates the financial and administrative responsibilities associated with professional contracting.

  • Business Organization: Understand business structures, administration, and operational responsibilities.
  • Accounting: Review financial statements, accounting principles, and recordkeeping.
  • Financial Management: Study cash flow, budgeting, and business financial planning.
  • Estimating and Bidding: Review project pricing, job costs, proposals, and estimating concepts.
  • Contracts: Understand construction agreements, contractual obligations, and administration.
  • Employee Management: Review payroll, personnel responsibilities, and business management practices.
  • Government Regulations: Reinforce knowledge of applicable contracting laws and regulatory responsibilities.

These subjects help candidates prepare for the business-related responsibilities associated with managing a plumbing contracting operation.

  • Materials, Uses, and Specifications – 6 Questions: Plumbing materials, fittings, joining methods, and installation requirements.
  • Traps, Interceptors, and Backwater Valves – 4 Questions: Fixture traps, interceptors, drainage protection, and backwater prevention.
  • Plumbing Fixtures, Fixture Fittings, and Plumbing Appliances – 4 Questions: Fixture installation, connections, and applicable requirements.
  • Water Supply Systems – 8 Questions: Water distribution, piping, supply protection, and installation principles.
  • Backflow Prevention – 10 Questions: Cross-connection protection and backflow prevention equipment.
  • Drain, Waste, and Vent Systems – 13 Questions: Sanitary drainage, venting, drainage piping, and system requirements.
  • Gas Appliances and Piping – 40 Questions: Fuel gas installations, appliance connections, piping, combustion air, and venting.
  • Plumbing Mathematics – 7 Questions: Trade calculations, dimensions, quantities, and mathematical problem-solving.

Gas Appliances and Piping is the largest examination category, accounting for 40% of the exam. Drain, Waste, and Vent Systems accounts for 13 questions, while Backflow Prevention represents 10 questions.

Understanding this distribution helps prioritize study time. Candidates should develop strong fuel gas knowledge while maintaining familiarity with every plumbing category.

Open Book Test

The Maryland Journey Plumber-Gas Fitter (PSI) examination is an open book test. Candidates may bring approved reference materials into the examination room under PSI testing rules.

The examination allows four hours for 100 questions. Knowing how to navigate approved references can help you manage your testing time more efficiently.

The approved reference materials include:

  • International Plumbing Code, 2018
  • International Fuel Gas Code, 2018
  • Mathematics for Plumbers and Pipefitters, 8th Edition, by Lee Smith
  • Any standard backflow text
  • Code of Federal Regulations - 29 CFR Part 1926 (OSHA), with current amendments, or the permitted PSI selections

PSI permits approved reference books containing highlighting, underlining, and acceptable indexing tabs. Books must not contain handwritten notes, additional loose papers, or attached study materials. Study guides are not permitted inside the testing room.

Reference materials are not supplied at the testing center, making familiarity with the books an important part of examination preparation.

Effective open-book study strategies include learning the organization of the plumbing and fuel gas codes, practicing reference navigation, reviewing important tables, and developing confidence interpreting technical requirements.

Licensing Steps

Maryland plumber and gas fitter licensing is regulated by the Maryland State Board of Plumbing. Applicants must meet the appropriate training and examination qualifications before receiving a journey-level license.

  1. Register as an Apprentice: Obtain the applicable Maryland apprentice plumber/gas fitter license.
  2. Complete Qualifying Training: Accumulate the required apprenticeship experience under the direction and control of a licensed master plumber.
  3. Complete Backflow Education: Fulfill the required backflow prevention device testing training.
  4. Document Your Qualifications: Organize apprenticeship records, experience verification, and training documentation.
  5. Apply Through PSI: Submit the examination application and supporting information through the online PSI examination system.
  6. Prepare for the Examination: Review the approved references and practice the nine examination subject areas.
  7. Schedule and Take the Test: Complete your examination after receiving the required approval.
  8. Apply for Licensure: Submit the Maryland journey plumber/gas fitter license application after satisfying the examination requirements.

Organizing your experience records, training documentation, and study schedule can help you approach both the examination and the licensing application process more efficiently.

State Requirements

The Maryland State Board of Plumbing establishes the qualifications for Journey Plumber/Gas Fitter licensing.

The established Maryland licensing pathway requires:

  • Four Years as an Apprentice: Applicants must have held an apprentice plumber/gas fitter license for at least four years.
  • 7,500 Hours of Training: Applicants must complete qualifying plumbing training under the direction and control of a licensed master plumber.
  • 32 Hours of Backflow Prevention Training: Completion of approved backflow prevention device testing training is required.
  • Passing Examination: Applicants must pass the comprehensive written examination.
  • Licensing Application: Applicants must submit the required information to the Maryland State Board of Plumbing.

Maryland examination guidance provides for credit toward qualifying experience from certain approved educational study. The examination application process requires documentation demonstrating eligibility.

A Maryland Journey Plumber/Gas Fitter performs plumbing and gas fitting work within the scope of the state's licensing rules and under the applicable direction and control of a licensed master plumber.

The journeyman credential represents an important stage in professional development, recognizing the knowledge and training needed to perform skilled plumbing and gas fitting work.

    Published by the International Code Council, the 2018 International Plumbing Code covers plumbing installation requirements, fixtures, water supply systems, sanitary drainage, vents, traps, interceptors, and related safety provisions. It provides important technical information for interpreting plumbing code questions and understanding plumbing system requirements.
  • International Fuel Gas Code, 2018
    The 2018 International Fuel Gas Code establishes requirements involving fuel gas piping systems, gas appliances, combustion air, venting, installation, and equipment safety. It is especially important for the Gas Appliances and Piping category, which represents 40 questions on the Maryland examination.
  • Mathematics for Plumbers and Pipefitters, 8th Edition
    Written by Lee Smith, this trade mathematics textbook explains calculations used in plumbing and pipefitting applications. It supports review of fractions, measurements, geometry, pipe-related calculations, and practical mathematical reasoning encountered in the plumbing trade.
  • Code of Federal Regulations - 29 CFR Part 1926 (OSHA)
    These federal construction safety regulations address workplace hazards, protective equipment, ladders, excavation, tools, fall protection, and other construction safety considerations. They help reinforce knowledge of safe work practices in plumbing and gas fitting environments.

California generally requires a qualifying individual to document at least four years of qualifying experience in the requested classification during the 10 years immediately before applying. Licensing Steps

The District of Columbia Board of Industrial Trades regulates plumbers and gasfitters in Washington DC. Candidates pursuing a Journeyman Plumber with Gas credential should satisfy the experience and application requirements that apply to journeyman-level plumbing and gasfitting work.

  1. Select the applicable combined plumbing and gasfitting credential. Washington DC regulates plumbing and gasfitting occupations and offers examinations covering both disciplines.
  2. Meet an approved journeyman qualification pathway. District law recognizes apprenticeship experience, qualifying engineering education with practical experience, comparable combinations of education and experience, and certain nationally certified apprenticeship pathways.
  3. Document qualifying experience. Applicants should maintain records supporting their plumbing and gasfitting work experience and any education or apprenticeship used for qualification.
  4. Submit the applicable District license application. Provide the information and supporting documentation required by the Board of Industrial Trades.
  5. Complete the examination authorization process. Candidates must satisfy the applicable licensing eligibility requirements before taking the examination.
  6. Prepare with both approved references. Study the 2012 International Plumbing Code and 2012 International Fuel Gas Code according to the current exam outline.
  7. Take the PSI examination. The current Journeyman Plumber with Gas exam contains 70 multiple-choice questions and allows four hours.
  8. Complete the remaining licensing requirements. Follow the Board of Industrial Trades requirements for completing the license process after satisfying the applicable examination and documentation requirements.

Passing the examination is only one part of the licensing process. Applicants must also satisfy the District's eligibility and documentation requirements for the credential being pursued.

State Requirements

Washington DC is a federal district rather than a state, but plumbers and gasfitters are regulated locally through the District of Columbia Board of Industrial Trades.

Under current District law, an applicant for licensure as a journeyman plumber or journeyman gasfitter may qualify by having worked as an apprentice plumber or gasfitter for at least 8,000 hours over at least four years.

The District also recognizes an education-based pathway for an applicant who has graduated from an accredited college or university with a degree in mechanical engineering and has at least two years of practical experience as a plumber or gasfitter verified by a licensed Master Plumber or licensed Master Gasfitter.

The Board may also recognize comparable experience or a combination of education and experience that it determines to be equivalent to the established pathways. Additional evidence may be required for a particular specialty license.

District law also recognizes a national-certification pathway. The Board may accept a qualifying certificate from a recognized national certifying organization when the applicant has completed the organization's apprenticeship program, passed its examination, holds the organization's journeyman designation, and remains in good standing under the applicable requirements.

The legal scope of plumbing in Washington DC includes installing, repairing, maintaining, and removing plumbing fixtures and piping associated with water supply and drainage systems. Gasfitting includes work involving nonindustrial gas appliances and piping systems from the applicable meter or service-regulator outlet to appliance connections.

Candidates pursuing a combined Journeyman Plumber with Gas credential should therefore prepare for both plumbing-system and fuel-gas responsibilities rather than studying only one discipline.

An individual journeyman trade license is also different from a Plumbing and Gasfitting Contractor license. A contracting business must separately satisfy the business licensing and contractor requirements that apply in the District.

Test Information and Study Materials

Plumbing Fixtures and Terminology account for 5% of the examination. Review plumbing definitions, fixture classifications, installation requirements, fixture connections, and terminology used throughout the International Plumbing Code.

Definitions are important because code questions often depend on precise terminology. Candidates should understand the difference between commonly confused plumbing terms and know where definitions can be located quickly.

Plumbing Fundamentals represent 13%. Study basic plumbing principles, general code requirements, piping materials, system operation, installation practices, calculations, and relationships among drainage, venting, water supply, fixtures, and traps.

Traps, Cleanouts, and Interceptors account for 4%. Review trap requirements, trap seals, prohibited configurations, cleanout placement, accessibility, interceptors, separators, and related plumbing provisions.

Special Requirements represent another 4%. These questions may address plumbing conditions or systems requiring additional code provisions beyond ordinary water, waste, and vent arrangements.

Drainage Requirements represent 14%. Candidates should review drainage fixture units, pipe sizing, horizontal and vertical drainage piping, building drains, building sewers, slopes, changes in direction, connections, and applicable sizing tables.

Drainage calculations deserve repeated practice. Candidates should be able to determine fixture-unit loads and select an appropriate pipe size from the correct IPC table.

Venting Requirements also represent 14%. Study individual vents, common vents, wet venting, circuit venting, vent sizing, vent connections, terminal requirements, and the relationship between traps and the venting system.

Plumbing venting should not be confused with fuel-gas appliance venting. Both are covered on this combined examination, but they are governed by different provisions and appear in different code books.

Water Distribution accounts for 12%. Review water-service piping, fixture supplies, water-distribution sizing, valves, pressure, backflow protection, water heaters, and potable-water system requirements.

Water-distribution questions may involve sizing, pressure, materials, system layout, or protection against contamination. Candidates should practice navigating between tables and the explanatory code sections surrounding them.

Plan Reading represents 14%. Candidates should be comfortable interpreting plumbing diagrams, identifying fixtures and piping, tracing drainage and vent systems, understanding water-distribution layouts, and applying code requirements to drawings.

A productive plan-reading strategy is to analyze one system at a time. Trace sanitary drainage first, then vents, water distribution, and gas piping. Breaking the drawing into systems can make complex plans easier to interpret.

Gas is the largest examination category at 20%. Candidates should devote substantial study time to the 2012 International Fuel Gas Code.

Review gas-piping materials, system installation, pipe sizing, shutoff valves, appliance connections, pressure considerations, combustion air, equipment installation, testing, and fuel-gas venting.

Gas-pipe sizing is an important calculation area. Practice selecting the correct table and using system length, connected demand, pressure, and other applicable factors to determine the required piping size.

Combustion air is another important subject. Candidates should understand the requirements for supplying adequate combustion, ventilation, and dilution air to fuel-burning appliances and know how to locate the applicable sizing methods.

Fuel-gas appliance venting should also receive dedicated attention. Review vent connectors, chimney and vent requirements, termination provisions, clearances, sizing, and appliance installation requirements.

The exam allows four hours for 70 questions, so candidates should use practice sessions to develop a consistent pace. Knowing which reference applies to a question before beginning the lookup can save significant time.

When a practice question is missed, identify the reason. The problem may involve selecting the wrong code book, choosing the wrong sizing table, misreading a plan, overlooking an exception, using the wrong fixture-unit value, or confusing plumbing venting with fuel-gas venting.

Repeated work with both approved references helps candidates build familiarity with code organization and table locations. Over time, common plumbing and gas subjects should become easier to find without broad searching.

This package gives candidates the technical resources needed to study those subjects in depth. Exam Details

The Chicago plumbing written examination is administered through Continental Testing Services as part of the City of Chicago plumbing licensing process.

The current written examination contains 100 questions and is timed for 3 hours. Candidates must earn a score of 70 or higher on the written test to pass and become eligible to take the Chicago Plumbing Practical Examination.

The current written examination content outline includes:

  • Plumbing Theory, Practices & Job Safety – 20 questions
  • Code Requirements for Plumbers & Contractors – 2 questions
  • Plumbing Systems – 49 questions
  • Drawings, Charts & Plans – 8 questions
  • Cutting & Assembling Plumbing System Components – 11 questions

Plumbing Systems is the largest examination category with 49 questions. This section covers the plumbing provisions contained in Chapter 18-29 of the Chicago Building Code, including administration, definitions, general regulations, fixtures, water heaters, water supply, sanitary drainage, indirect and special waste, vents, traps, separators, interceptors, storm drainage, and swimming pools.

Plumbing Theory, Practices & Job Safety accounts for 20 questions. Candidates should be prepared for plumbing mathematics, public-health principles, planning, tools, equipment, basic electricity, workplace safety, and OSHA-related subjects.

The Chicago Journeyman Plumber licensing process includes both written and practical examinations as well as documented apprentice experience.

  1. Complete qualifying apprenticeship experience. Current examination requirements call for four years of work as a Plumber's Apprentice.
  2. Maintain the required apprentice credential. Applicants must provide a copy of their applicable apprentice license as part of the examination documentation.
  3. Obtain employer verification. Candidates must provide an original signed letter from a current or former employer that is a licensed and bonded plumbing contractor.
  4. Document employment dates and experience. The employer letter must establish that the applicant completed the required four years of apprentice plumbing work and include the contractor's license information.
  5. Apply for the Chicago Journeyman Plumber examination. Complete the required City of Chicago and Continental Testing Services application process.
  6. Prepare for the written examination. Study Chicago plumbing-code provisions, theory, calculations, safety, plans, installation practices, system components, troubleshooting, and repair.
  7. Pass the written examination. Candidates must score 70 or higher to become eligible for the practical examination.
  8. Complete the Chicago Plumbing Practical Examination. The practical examination evaluates drawing and piping-assembly skills.
  9. Pass the required practical components. Candidates must achieve the required score on each practical examination component.
  10. Complete the licensing process. After meeting the written, practical, experience, and application requirements, complete the remaining City of Chicago requirements for Journeyman Plumber licensure.

The verification letter must establish the dates of employment and confirm completion of the required apprentice experience. It must also include the employer's plumbing contractor license number, and the applicant must provide a copy of the apprentice license.

Candidates currently licensed as an Apprentice Plumber by either the City of Chicago or the State of Illinois may apply through the applicable current examination process.

The licensing examination has two stages. Candidates first pass the written examination and then proceed to the Chicago Plumbing Practical Examination. Both are required parts of the professional licensing process.

The practical examination contains two major components. One requires candidates to complete plumbing specifications for a three-story residential building by adding required sewer, drain, waste, and vent piping, including an overhead sewer with an ejector system, in accordance with the current Chicago Plumbing Code.

The second practical component involves a copper pipe assembly project. Candidates must interpret a drawing, calculate required tubing dimensions, measure and cut tubing, assemble the specified sections, and solder the completed project.

  1. Work as a licensed Apprentice Plumber. Build qualifying residential plumbing experience within Utah's licensing and supervision requirements.
  2. Follow an approved qualification pathway. Utah provides an apprenticeship education pathway and an experience-based pathway for Residential Journeyman Plumber applicants.

Utah's Residential Journeyman Plumber licensing requirements include approved apprenticeship education and documented work experience. The standard licensure pathway requires at least 432 hours of approved apprenticeship education and 6,000 hours of qualifying apprentice plumbing experience.

The G27 National Standard Master Plumber with Gas examination combines a broad Master Plumber knowledge base with fuel-gas system requirements. Candidates should be prepared to work with general plumbing regulations, code terminology, plan reading, testing, approved materials, plumbing fixtures, potable water systems, sanitary drainage, venting, traps, interceptors, separators, storm drainage, gas piping, combustion air, gas appliances, and fuel-gas venting.

Candidates need to understand how plumbing systems are installed and tested while also being able to evaluate fuel-gas piping, equipment connections, combustion-air provisions, and venting requirements. Strong preparation requires familiarity with both references and the ability to determine which code applies to the condition described in a question.

The 2018 International Plumbing Code provides the primary requirements for plumbing systems, including fixtures, water supply, sanitary drainage, vents, traps, special waste, and storm drainage. The 2018 International Fuel Gas Code addresses gas piping, fuel-burning appliances, combustion air, vents, connectors, and related fuel-gas installation requirements.

Online practice questions help turn these references into working study tools. Candidates can use each question to identify the subject, select the correct code book, locate the applicable provision or table, and apply the requirement to the installation scenario presented.

Exam Details

The ICC G27 National Standard Master Plumber with Gas examination contains 100 multiple-choice questions and has a 4-hour time limit.

The official G27 examination outline divides the test into eight major content areas:

  • Administration General Regulations – 36%
  • Plumbing Fixtures – 13%
  • Water Supply and Distribution – 9%
  • Sanitary Drainage – 8%
  • Plumbing Vent Requirements – 6%
  • Traps, Interceptors, and Separators – 5%
  • Storm Drainage – 2%
  • Gas Piping – 21%

Administration General Regulations is the largest content area at 36%. This portion includes general installation requirements, code definitions and terms, plan reading, testing, and materials. Candidates should devote significant preparation time to this area because these fundamentals affect many different plumbing and fuel-gas installations.

Gas Piping is the second-largest content area at 21%. This portion covers gas piping for service and distribution, gas-piping requirements associated with specific appliances and equipment, sources of combustion air and duct openings, and requirements involving fuel-burning appliances, vents, and connectors.

Plumbing Fixtures represent 13% of the examination and include water heaters, water closets and urinals, specialty fixtures, bathtubs, showers, sinks, and lavatories.

Water Supply and Distribution account for 9% and include service distribution and piping, water supply and pressure, and protection of the potable water supply.

Sanitary Drainage represents 8% of the test and includes building sanitary drainage, sumps and ejectors, and indirect and special waste systems.

Plumbing Vent Requirements account for 6%, while Traps, Interceptors, and Separators account for 5%. Storm Drainage represents the remaining 2% of the official examination outline.

Open Book Test

The ICC G27 National Standard Master Plumber with Gas examination is an open book test. Candidates have four hours to complete 100 multiple-choice questions and must follow current ICC examination rules regarding allowable reference materials.

The open-book format makes familiarity with both the IPC and IFGC especially important. Candidates should be able to determine quickly whether a question belongs in the plumbing code or fuel-gas code before searching for the answer.

A question involving drainage fixture units, sanitary piping, plumbing vents, traps, water supply, or plumbing fixtures should generally direct attention toward the 2018 International Plumbing Code. Questions involving gas-pipe sizing, fuel-gas distribution, combustion air, appliance venting, or gas connectors should direct attention toward the 2018 International Fuel Gas Code.

Candidates should practice identifying the correct chapter and table before beginning a detailed search. This can save significant time during a 100-question exam.

The G27 examination allows approximately two minutes and twenty-four seconds per question on average. Some questions may be answered from experience or code familiarity, while others may require a detailed table lookup, calculation, or plan interpretation.

Use practice questions as reference-navigation exercises. After selecting an answer, locate the supporting provision and review nearby exceptions, definitions, notes, and tables. That habit helps build the familiarity needed for efficient open-book testing.

Licensing Steps

The G27 is an ICC National Standard contractor/trades examination. ICC administers the examination, while individual states and local jurisdictions determine whether it is accepted or required for a Master Plumber with Gas license or similar credential.

  1. Identify the required license classification. Determine whether the G27 National Standard Master Plumber with Gas exam is required or accepted by the jurisdiction where you intend to work.
  2. Review jurisdiction requirements. Confirm any application, experience, business, or other qualifications imposed by the applicable licensing authority.
  3. Prepare with the correct references. This product uses the 2018 International Plumbing Code and 2018 International Fuel Gas Code.
  4. Study by official exam category. Divide preparation among general regulations, fixtures, water supply, sanitary drainage, plumbing vents, traps and interceptors, storm drainage, and gas piping.
  5. Practice plan reading. Develop the ability to interpret plumbing layouts and connect plan information to applicable code requirements.
  6. Strengthen gas-code navigation. Practice locating gas-piping, combustion-air, appliance, vent, and connector requirements quickly.
  7. Use the online practice questions. Work through exam-focused questions throughout the included 3-month access period.
  8. Register for the G27 exam. Follow the applicable ICC examination registration and scheduling process.
  9. Complete the examination. Answer the 100 multiple-choice questions within the 4-hour testing period.
  10. Complete remaining jurisdiction requirements. Follow any additional steps required by the authority issuing the applicable license or credential.

State Requirements

The ICC G27 National Standard Master Plumber with Gas examination is a national contractor/trades examination. It provides a standardized technical examination but does not itself create a nationwide plumbing or gas license.

States, counties, municipalities, and other licensing jurisdictions determine whether the G27 examination is accepted for their licensing programs. Requirements may differ significantly depending on where a candidate intends to perform plumbing or fuel-gas work.

Passing the G27 exam and obtaining a license are therefore separate matters. The examination measures technical knowledge, while the applicable jurisdiction determines eligibility, experience requirements, applications, and other licensing conditions.

Candidates pursuing licensure should identify the exact classification they need and confirm that the G27 examination satisfies the applicable trade-examination requirement.

The open-book format makes efficient code navigation an important part of preparation. Candidates should become familiar enough with the 2018 International Plumbing Code to know where major subjects are located before beginning a detailed search.

The 2018 International Plumbing Code should be used throughout preparation as a working reference. Candidates should understand where to locate general regulations, plumbing fixtures, water heaters, water supply and distribution, sanitary drainage, indirect and special waste, vents, traps, interceptors, separators, and storm drainage.

A water-pressure or potable-water protection question should direct attention toward water supply and distribution provisions. A question about building drains, drainage fixture units, cleanouts, or ejectors should point toward sanitary drainage requirements. Venting questions should lead toward the venting provisions, while trap or interceptor questions should direct attention to the applicable trap and special waste sections.

Because candidates have four hours for 70 questions, there is more time per question than on many ICC contractor exams. Even so, inefficient searching can consume valuable testing time. Candidates who understand how the IPC is organized can use that time more effectively on questions involving detailed tables, sizing, plan interpretation, or multiple code requirements.

Practice questions can be used as code-navigation exercises. After answering a question, locate the applicable IPC section and review nearby provisions. This helps reinforce both the specific rule and the structure of the plumbing code.

Licensing Steps

The G25 is an ICC National Standard contractor/trades examination. ICC administers the examination program, while individual licensing jurisdictions determine whether the G25 exam is accepted or required for a Journeyman Plumber credential.

  1. Identify the applicable Journeyman Plumber requirement. Determine whether the G25 National Standard Journeyman Plumber exam is required or accepted by the jurisdiction where you intend to work.
  2. Review jurisdiction-specific requirements. Confirm any experience, application, registration, or other requirements established by the applicable licensing authority.
  3. Prepare with the correct reference. This preparation product uses the 2018 International Plumbing Code.
  4. Study by examination content area. Organize study around Administration General Regulations, Plumbing Fixtures, Water Supply and Distribution, Sanitary Drainage, Plumbing Vent Requirements, Traps and Interceptors, and Storm Drainage.
  5. Practice plan reading. Develop familiarity with plumbing layouts and how information shown on plans connects to code requirements.
  6. Build IPC navigation skills. Practice locating applicable sections, tables, definitions, materials, testing provisions, and sizing requirements efficiently.
  7. Use the online practice questions. Work through exam-oriented plumbing scenarios and revisit weaker subjects throughout the 3-month access period.
  8. Register for the G25 examination. Follow the current ICC contractor/trades examination registration and scheduling process.
  9. Complete the examination. Answer the 70 multiple-choice questions within the 4-hour testing period.
  10. Complete applicable licensing requirements. Follow the remaining requirements established by the jurisdiction where you are pursuing a Journeyman Plumber credential.

State Requirements

The ICC G25 National Standard Journeyman Plumber examination is a national contractor/trades examination. It provides participating jurisdictions with a standardized way to evaluate plumbing knowledge, but the examination itself is not a nationwide Journeyman Plumber license.

State and local governments determine licensing requirements for plumbers. Depending on the jurisdiction, a candidate may need to satisfy requirements beyond passing the G25 examination before receiving permission to work under a regulated Journeyman Plumber classification.

The appropriate licensing authority determines whether the ICC G25 exam is accepted, how examination results are used, and what additional qualifications apply. Candidates should follow the specific rules of the jurisdiction where they plan to obtain a plumbing credential.

The G25 examination focuses on technical plumbing knowledge using the 2018 IPC. It evaluates the candidate's ability to understand general requirements, installations, fixtures, water supply, sanitary drainage, venting, traps, interceptors, separators, storm drainage, testing, materials, and plumbing plans.

Begin with Administration General Regulations because it represents 40% of the exam. Review general installation requirements, materials, testing, code definitions, terminology, and plan reading. These subjects form the foundation for many plumbing questions and should be studied throughout the preparation period.

General Installation Requirements can involve piping support, protection, approved installation methods, system location, workmanship, connections, and other broad requirements that affect plumbing systems. Understanding these general provisions can help candidates solve questions across several code chapters.

Code Definitions and Terms should not be overlooked. Plumbing codes use precise definitions for fixtures, piping components, drainage systems, vents, waste types, and other technical concepts. Correctly interpreting the terminology in a question can be essential to identifying the applicable code requirement.

Plan Reading is part of the Administration General Regulations category. Candidates should practice identifying fixtures, piping arrangements, pipe sizes, system connections, and other information on plumbing plans. The goal is to connect what appears on the drawing with the appropriate IPC requirement.

Testing is another part of this heavily weighted category. Review the plumbing-code provisions associated with testing completed systems and components before systems are placed into service or concealed where applicable.

For Plumbing Fixtures, review water heaters, water closets, urinals, specialty fixtures, fixture connections, and installation requirements. Candidates should understand how fixture installation interacts with water supply, drainage, clearances, and other plumbing provisions.

For Water Supply and Distribution, study service distribution and piping, available pressure, distribution-system sizing, valves, potable-water protection, backflow prevention, and other requirements affecting safe water delivery.

Water-supply questions may involve several steps. Candidates may need to identify the fixture demand, determine system conditions, locate the applicable table, and interpret the result correctly. Practicing table navigation can improve both accuracy and speed.

For Sanitary Drainage, review building drains, drainage fixture units, pipe sizing, horizontal drainage, stacks, cleanouts, slope, sumps, ejectors, indirect waste, and special waste. Candidates should understand how fixtures discharge into a properly sized and arranged drainage system.

For Plumbing Vent Requirements, study vent connections, grades, terminals, sizing principles, and the relationship between venting and trap-seal protection. Candidates should become familiar with acceptable vent arrangements and conditions that affect vent installation.

For Traps, Interceptors, and Separators, review required traps, trap installation, trap seals, prohibited arrangements, interceptors, separators, and applications where special devices are required before waste enters the drainage system.

Use missed questions to guide additional study. If water-supply sizing is difficult, spend more time with the applicable tables. If venting questions cause problems, review vent arrangements and termination requirements. If plan-reading questions take too long, practice identifying system components before opening the code.

The strongest study routine combines technical review with repeated reference navigation. Instead of memorizing only a correct answer, find the supporting code provision and understand why it applies. That process helps build knowledge that can transfer to new questions on the examination.

Applicants must satisfy one of several experience pathways. One primary pathway requires at least seven years of total qualifying experience within the ten years before application involving installation of plumbing systems and the planning or design of plumbing systems under the direct and continuing supervision of a Licensed Master Plumber in the United States. Under that pathway, at least two years of the qualifying experience must be completed as a registered journeyman plumber as required by applicable New York City provisions.

Other pathways are available for candidates with qualifying mechanical engineering or engineering technology education, New York State-licensed Registered Architects or Professional Engineers, certain city-agency plumbing experience, and qualifying plumbing inspection experience.

The Department requires candidates to pass both the written and practical examinations before submitting the background application for the license. The current written examination passing requirement is 70%.

After successfully completing the examination process, applicants must submit the required licensing documentation and complete the Department's background investigation. The licensing application is submitted through DOB NOW: Licensing.

Passing the examinations does not automatically result in license issuance. Applicants must also satisfy the applicable experience, documentation, fitness, character, background, and license application requirements.

Reference Books

  • 2022 NYC Administrative Code, Title 28, Chapter 1: Administration; Chapter 2: Enforcement; Chapter 3: Maintenance of Buildings
    Supports preparation involving administration of the New York City Construction Codes, enforcement procedures, responsibilities, violations, compliance, and building maintenance requirements relevant to licensed plumbing work.
  • 2022 NYC Construction Codes: Building Code
    Supports study of broader building requirements that can affect plumbing installations, including construction conditions, penetrations, shafts, fire-resistance features, occupancy-related requirements, and coordination with other building systems.
  • 2022 NYC Construction Codes: Fuel Gas Code
    Supports preparation involving fuel gas piping systems, materials, sizing, installation, pressure testing, appliances, combustion air, vents, chimneys, equipment connections, and fuel gas safety requirements.
  • 2022 NYC Construction Codes: Plumbing Code
    Supports comprehensive preparation involving plumbing fixtures, sanitary drainage, venting, water supply and distribution, storm drainage, traps, cleanouts, interceptors, piping materials, installation requirements, and plumbing system design principles.

Test Information and Study Materials

A strong New York Master Plumber study plan should begin with the 2022 NYC Plumbing Code. Candidates should understand the organization of plumbing systems even though the book cannot be used during the examination.

Sanitary drainage should receive substantial attention. Study drainage system layout, fixture units, horizontal and vertical piping, slope, cleanouts, building drains, building sewers, branches, stacks, and connections between system components.

Venting is another essential subject. Candidates should understand the purpose of vent systems and how venting protects trap seals and supports proper drainage system operation. Review individual vents, common vents, circuit venting, wet venting, stack venting, vent sizing, and termination principles.

Water supply and distribution should be studied from both a design and installation perspective. Review water service, distribution piping, pressure, sizing, valves, backflow protection, water heaters, and relationships between demand and pipe capacity.

Plumbing fixtures should include fixture requirements, connections, installation, accessibility considerations, and the relationship between fixture counts and building use.

Traps, interceptors, and separators should be reviewed carefully. Candidates should understand their purpose, location, installation, maintenance, and relationship to the drainage system.

Storm drainage should also be included in preparation. Review roof drainage concepts, leaders, conductors, storm piping, sizing considerations, and methods used to direct stormwater away from buildings.

The 2022 NYC Fuel Gas Code should receive dedicated study rather than being treated as a secondary reference. Candidates should understand gas piping materials, sizing concepts, installation, pressure testing, appliance connections, shutoff valves, combustion air, venting, and safe fuel gas practices.

Combustion air and venting are particularly important because improper installation can create serious hazards. Candidates should understand how appliances receive adequate combustion air and how combustion products are safely removed.

The 2022 NYC Building Code should be studied for requirements that interact with plumbing work. Plumbing systems pass through walls, floors, shafts, ceilings, and other building elements, making coordination with broader building requirements necessary.

The Administrative Code should be reviewed for licensing, enforcement, responsibility, and maintenance provisions. A Master Plumber must understand not only how systems are installed but also the professional and regulatory framework surrounding licensed work.

Because the examination is closed book, candidates should avoid relying entirely on passive reading. Use active recall, written practice, system diagrams, and problem-solving exercises to build stronger retained knowledge.

One effective method is to draw a complete plumbing system from memory. Include the water service, distribution lines, fixtures, traps, sanitary drainage, vents, building drain, and building sewer. Then compare the drawing against applicable code requirements.

Do the same for fuel gas systems. Trace the system from the point of supply through distribution piping to appliances and identify the valves, piping considerations, combustion air, and venting requirements that affect safe operation.

Practice should also include calculations and sizing exercises where applicable. Plumbing examinations often require candidates to combine technical rules with tables, system demand, fixture loads, piping relationships, and practical installation knowledge.

Mixed-topic practice is especially useful during the final stage of preparation. Move between drainage, venting, water supply, fuel gas, fixtures, storm drainage, Building Code requirements, and administrative responsibilities rather than studying one subject exclusively.

When a practice question is missed, determine why. The problem may involve an unfamiliar code requirement, incorrect system reasoning, confusion between similar plumbing methods, or weak understanding of a calculation. Review the underlying concept before returning to practice.

The practical examination should also influence study. Candidates should develop a working understanding of plumbing systems rather than memorizing isolated code sentences. A strong Master Plumber should be able to identify a system, understand how its parts interact, and recognize whether an installation follows applicable New York City requirements.

Does the licensing process include both written and practical exams?
