  • Vents: 22%

Sanitary Drainage is the largest single category at 23% of the examination. Candidates should be familiar with drainage piping, sizing, slope, cleanouts, building drains, fixture drains, branches, stacks, materials, connections, and installation requirements.

Water Supply and Distribution and Vents each represent 22%. Together with Sanitary Drainage, these three categories account for more than two-thirds of the examination content.

General Requirements account for 14%. This category can include permits, piping protection, approved materials, inspections, testing, structural protection, and general installation requirements.

Water Heaters represent 11%, while Fixtures account for 8%. Candidates should prepare for questions involving water-heater installation, temperature and pressure protection, fixture requirements, connections, clearances, and approved plumbing components.

Open Book Test

The ICC Residential Plumbing Inspector examination is an open-book test.

For the 2021 examination version, the required reference is the International Residential Code, 2021. Candidates may use approved references during the exam in accordance with ICC testing rules.

Open-book testing still requires efficient preparation. With 60 questions and a 2-hour limit, candidates have an average of about 2 minutes per question. Searching randomly through the IRC for every answer can consume valuable time.

A better strategy is to identify the plumbing subject before opening the code. A drainage question should immediately point toward sanitary drainage provisions. A venting question should direct attention to the vent chapters, while a fixture or water-heater question should suggest a different area of the IRC.

Practice should also include using the code's index, tables, definitions, and cross-references. Many inspection questions require candidates to find a specific dimensional requirement, sizing rule, material limitation, or exception.

During preparation, attempt each practice question before looking up the answer. Then use the IRC to confirm the applicable requirement. This strengthens both plumbing knowledge and code-navigation ability.

Licensing Steps

  1. Confirm the Florida Residential Plumbing Inspector certification category. Florida regulates building code inspectors by inspection discipline and category.
  2. Meet the applicable qualification requirements. Applicants must qualify through an accepted experience, education, certification, or Board-approved training pathway.
  3. Submit the appropriate Florida application. Building code inspector applications are processed through the Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation.
  4. Receive approval for the required examinations. Candidates must satisfy the state's application requirements before completing the necessary examination process.
  5. Prepare for the ICC Residential Plumbing Inspector examination. Study the 2021 International Residential Code and the official plumbing inspector content areas.
  6. Take the ICC 1P technical examination. The exam contains 60 multiple-choice questions and provides 2 hours.
  7. Complete the Florida Principles and Practice examination. Florida applicants seeking inspector certification by examination must also satisfy the separate state examination requirement.
  8. Complete remaining certification requirements. Florida reviews examination results and all required application, experience, education, training, and certification documentation before issuing a license.

State Requirements

Residential Plumbing Inspectors in Florida are regulated through the Building Code Administrators and Inspectors Board under the Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation.

Florida requires building code inspectors to hold certification in the inspection category in which they work. Residential Plumbing Inspector certification applies to residential plumbing inspections within the applicable state and code scope.

Applicants seeking initial certification by examination must meet one of Florida's approved qualification pathways. These may involve construction or inspection experience, post-secondary education combined with experience, existing certifications, or Board-approved training programs.

Florida's experience-based pathways include qualifying construction or inspection work in the category sought. Other routes allow combinations of post-secondary education and experience or additional approved qualifications.

Florida applicants seeking certification by examination must pass an appropriate International Code Council technical examination and the separate Florida Principles and Practice examination.

The ICC Residential Plumbing Inspector exam addressed by this product is the technical examination component. Candidates preparing for Florida licensure should plan separately for the Florida Principles and Practice examination.

Florida currently makes ICC National Certification examinations available to Florida candidates through the PRONTO remote-proctored testing platform. The Florida Principles and Practice examination continues to be available through Florida's separate approved testing process.

Passing the ICC technical examination alone does not automatically issue a Florida Residential Plumbing Inspector certification. Applicants must also satisfy the applicable experience, education or training, application, state examination, and other certification requirements.

Reference Books

  • International Residential Code, 2021
    The required reference for the 2021 Residential Plumbing Inspector examination. It supports preparation involving general plumbing requirements, fixtures, water heaters, water supply and distribution, sanitary drainage, vents, piping materials, testing, and other residential plumbing inspection requirements.

Test Information and Study Materials

A strong ICC Residential Plumbing Inspector study plan should begin with the three largest content areas: Sanitary Drainage, Water Supply and Distribution, and Vents.

Sanitary Drainage represents 23% of the examination. Candidates should understand how wastewater moves through residential piping systems and how the IRC regulates sizing, slope, materials, cleanouts, connections, and installation.

Review fixture drains, branch drains, drainage stacks, building drains, building sewers, cleanout locations, drainage fittings, and approved piping materials.

Drainage inspection questions often require candidates to determine whether a piping arrangement, size, slope, or fitting is acceptable. Practice identifying the specific condition in the question before selecting a code section.

Water Supply and Distribution represents 22%. Candidates should review potable water piping, distribution systems, pressure, materials, valves, connections, fixture supply, protection against contamination, and sizing concepts.

Residential plumbing inspectors should understand how water enters a dwelling and is distributed to fixtures and equipment. Questions can involve pipe sizing, pressure, protection, materials, accessibility, and installation conditions.

Backflow protection and cross-connection control are important water-supply concepts. Candidates should understand how potable water systems are protected from contamination and which installations require protective devices or methods.

Vents also represent 22%. Vent systems protect trap seals and support proper drainage-system performance. Candidates should understand vent sizing, vent connections, vent terminations, wet venting, individual vents, common vents, and other permitted arrangements.

Venting questions can be challenging because the answer may depend on both the fixture arrangement and pipe size. Practice visualizing the complete system instead of focusing only on a single pipe.

General Requirements account for 14%. This category includes broader plumbing inspection responsibilities such as permits, testing, approved materials, piping protection, structural protection, and installation requirements.

Piping must be protected from physical damage, corrosion, freezing, stress, and strain. Candidates should understand how plumbing installations interact with building framing and how the code protects both the piping and the structure.

Water Heaters represent 11%. Study water-heater installation, location, temperature and pressure relief protection, discharge piping, connections, clearances, pans, supports, and other applicable residential requirements.

Water-heater questions may require close attention to the installation condition. A requirement can differ depending on location, fuel type, surrounding construction, or equipment configuration.

Fixtures account for 8%. Review fixture materials, required fixtures, clearances, installation, supports, connections, faucets, traps, and fixture-specific requirements.

Inspection-focused preparation should include recognizing whether fixtures are properly installed, accessible, supported, connected, and supplied with appropriate drainage and water connections.

The 2021 International Residential Code should be used actively throughout preparation. Practice locating plumbing requirements by topic rather than trying to memorize the entire code.

One effective method is to read a practice question and identify the main keyword. Terms such as cleanout, trap, vent, fixture, water heater, supply piping, or drainage stack can help point toward the correct chapter or section.

Tables deserve special attention. Plumbing codes frequently use tables for pipe sizing, fixture-unit relationships, developed lengths, spacing, and other requirements. Practice reading both table headings and footnotes carefully.

Definitions can also affect the correct answer. Plumbing terminology is precise, and two similar words may refer to different parts of a system. When a question seems ambiguous, checking the code definition can help clarify the intended meaning.

When a practice question is missed, determine why. The issue may be weak code navigation, misunderstanding of system operation, overlooking a table note, confusing drainage with vent requirements, or missing an exception.

Organize missed questions by category. If sanitary drainage remains difficult, focus additional study there. If venting or water distribution produces repeated errors, dedicate separate review sessions to those topics.

As preparation progresses, combine categories into mixed-question sets. A realistic exam may switch from a water-heater question to drainage, then fixtures, vents, water supply, or general requirements.

Because the exam contains 60 questions in 2 hours, time management matters. Candidates should answer familiar questions efficiently and preserve extra time for complicated code lookups or table interpretation.

The Arizona Registrar of Contractors administers contractor licensing in Arizona, while PSI provides the trade-specific contractor examination program. Open Book Test

Is the Arizona R-37R plumbing exam open book?

How many questions are on the R-37R examination?

The Arizona R-37R Plumbing Residential trade examination contains 100 questions.

How much time is allowed for the exam?

Candidates are allowed 240 minutes to complete the R-37R trade examination.

What score is required to pass?

The minimum passing score is 70 percent.

Who administers the Arizona contractor trade exam?

PSI administers Arizona’s trade-specific contractor examinations under the state contractor testing program. The Arizona Registrar of Contractors is responsible for reviewing contractor license applications and issuing licenses.

State Requirements

The C-77 Plumbing, Including Solar Commercial classification includes installation, alteration, and repair of all plumbing, including solar, when performed solely within property lines and not on public easements or rights-of-way except as allowed by the classification.

The scope includes piping, fixtures, and appliances related to water supply, including pressure vessels and tanks, excluding municipal or related water supply systems. It also includes venting and sanitary drainage systems for fluid, semi-fluid, and organic wastes; septic tanks and leaching lines; roof leaders; lawn sprinkler systems; water conditioning equipment; and piping and equipment for swimming pools.

The classification also includes piping, fixtures, appliances, and pressure vessels for manufactured and natural gases, compressed air and vacuum systems, petroleum, fuel oil, non-potable liquids, hot water heating and hot water supply systems operating at pressures not exceeding 30 psig or temperatures not exceeding 220°F, steam heating and steam supply systems not exceeding 15 psig operating pressure, and gas- or oil-fired space heaters and furnaces excluding duct work. It also includes piping for water cooling systems excluding refrigerant piping and equipment, plus testing and balancing of hydronic systems.

Sewer, gas, and water lines and connections from a structure to the nearest point of public supply or disposal may cross public or private easements or be installed within private easements. Pipe installed across public property may not be increased in size or make another connection between the point of exit from private property and the point of connection at public supply or disposal. State Requirements

The North Carolina State Board of Examiners of Electrical Contractors administers electrical contractor licensing in North Carolina. The Board regulates electrical contractor classifications, examinations, licensing, renewals, and discipline under North Carolina electrical contracting law and Board rules.

The Special Restricted Plumbing and Heating electrical contracting license, identified as SP-PH, authorizes the licensee to install, maintain, or repair electric wiring or devices only as an incident to the licensee’s plumbing, heating, or air conditioning business. This classification is limited in scope and is not the same as a Limited, Intermediate, or Unlimited electrical contractor license.

The state scope for the SP-PH classification limits the licensee to wiring directly related to plumbing, heating, or air conditioning equipment. The wiring is restricted to circuits or parts of circuits that operate at voltages not exceeding 600 volts phase-to-phase. Candidates should understand the role of overcurrent protective isolating devices, equipment identification, equipment enclosures, and the point where the special restricted contractor’s work may begin.

The SP-PH classification also includes limitations tied to electrical work involving equipment served by plumbing, heating, or air conditioning systems. Candidates should understand that the license does not authorize unrestricted electrical contracting or general electrical work outside the classification scope. These scope limits are important for both exam preparation and real-world compliance.

North Carolina electrical contracting licenses issued by the Board expire one year after issuance. Licensees are responsible for renewing on time and keeping license information current. Anyone pursuing the SP-PH classification should review Board licensing procedures, renewal responsibilities, classification limits, and contractor requirements before operating as a licensed electrical contractor.

The classification applies to solar plumbing liquid systems used in commercial settings and focuses on solar water heating work that uses liquid as the transfer medium.

The scope of work includes the installation, alteration, and repair of solar water heating systems operating at temperatures not exceeding 220 degrees Fahrenheit. The scope excludes non-solar plumbing, electrical, and mechanical systems and components.

Tennessee's current LLP guidance states that general maintenance work costing less than $500 is exempt from the LLP license requirement. Other exemptions and local requirements may apply depending on the individual, employer, location, and nature of the work.

The LLP license differs from Tennessee's contractor-level plumbing classifications. Candidates who plan to undertake plumbing projects at or above the contractor licensing threshold should understand whether a different Tennessee contractor classification is required for their intended work.

Local government requirements remain important even after a state LLP license is issued. Municipalities or counties may impose additional licensing, permit, inspection, or code requirements. Candidates preparing for the LLP exam should consider the state license one part of the broader process of performing plumbing work legally and professionally.

Reference Books

  • International Plumbing Code, 2021
    A primary plumbing-code reference covering water supply and distribution, sanitary drainage, vent systems, fixtures, traps, water heaters, piping materials, indirect waste, storm drainage, and other plumbing requirements. The 2021 International Plumbing Code is currently identified by Prov as a primary LLP examination reference.
  • Mathematics for Plumbers and Pipefitters, 8th Edition
    A trade mathematics resource covering calculations relevant to plumbing and pipefitting work. It supports preparation involving measurement, dimensions, formulas, practical arithmetic, pipe-related calculations, and other mathematical concepts encountered in the plumbing trade. The 8th Edition is currently identified by Prov as a primary LLP examination reference.
  • Plumbing Basics for Contractors
    A contractor-focused plumbing reference supporting review of practical plumbing systems, water supply, drainage, venting, fixtures, piping, terminology, installation principles, and general plumbing trade knowledge. Prov's current reference list identifies Plumbing Basics for Contractors, 4th Edition, 2021 for the LLP examination.
  • International Fuel Gas Code, 2021
    A fuel-gas code reference covering gas piping, piping materials, system sizing, appliance installation, combustion air, venting, chimneys, and related fuel-gas requirements. This book provides additional study support for the Fuel Gas Systems portion of the LLP exam.
  • Code of Federal Regulations - 29 CFR Part 1926 (OSHA)
    A construction safety reference covering federal OSHA requirements for construction workplaces. Topics include personal protective equipment, ladders, scaffolds, excavation, fall protection, tools, electrical hazards, and other jobsite safety provisions that support preparation for the OSHA Safety portion of the LLP exam.

Test Information and Study Materials

A productive LLP study plan should begin with the largest areas of the current examination. Drain, Waste, and Vent Systems accounts for one-quarter of the 40-question exam. Candidates should become familiar with sanitary drainage, drainage fittings, vent systems, traps, cleanouts, materials, sizing concepts, and the sections of the International Plumbing Code where these requirements are located.

Isometrics accounts for 7 questions and deserves dedicated practice. Plumbing isometric questions can require candidates to visualize piping systems and interpret relationships among fixtures, drainage piping, vents, and other components. Practice reading plumbing drawings and following piping paths rather than relying exclusively on text-based study.

Water Supply and Distribution and Code Requirements each contain 4 questions. The International Plumbing Code, 2021 should be used regularly during preparation for these subjects. Candidates should learn how chapters are organized and practice using code tables, definitions, exceptions, and index terms.

Fuel Gas Systems also accounts for 4 questions. The International Fuel Gas Code, 2021 provides additional study material involving fuel-gas piping, sizing, materials, appliances, combustion air, vents, and related system requirements. Candidates can use this reference to strengthen technical understanding while preparing for fuel-gas questions.

Mathematics for Plumbers and Pipefitters, 8th Edition supports the Plumbing Math portion of the examination. Candidates should actively solve problems involving measurements and plumbing-related calculations instead of only reading worked examples. Repetition helps build speed and reduces the likelihood of basic calculation errors under testing conditions.

OSHA Safety accounts for 2 questions. Code of Federal Regulations - 29 CFR Part 1926 gives candidates a broader construction-safety resource for studying hazards and safe work practices relevant to plumbing and construction jobsites.

The remaining exam areas include General Knowledge, Water Heaters, and Fixtures & Fittings. These sections should be incorporated into a complete study routine. Candidates should review terminology, installation principles, fixture concepts, water-heater requirements, and other practical plumbing knowledge connected to these subjects.

Reference navigation should be practiced throughout preparation. A useful method is to read a question, identify the topic, decide which reference is most appropriate, locate the relevant chapter or index term, and confirm the answer. Practicing this process repeatedly can help candidates become more efficient with their books before taking the open-book examination.

How 1 Exam Prep Helps You Reach Your Goal

1 Exam Prep helps Tennessee Limited Licensed Plumber candidates organize their preparation around the trade knowledge and reference-navigation skills needed for the LLP examination. Instead of approaching the exam as a collection of unrelated plumbing topics, candidates can build a structured study plan around the published subject areas and the references that support them.

Our approach emphasizes plumbing-focused review, practice-oriented preparation, efficient use of code books, and familiarity with trade references. Candidates can strengthen their understanding of drainage and venting, water distribution, plumbing math, fixtures, isometrics, fuel gas, safety, and other plumbing concepts while learning where important information is located.

Open-book preparation works best when candidates repeatedly use their books before the exam. Learning the structure of the International Plumbing Code, practicing calculations with Mathematics for Plumbers and Pipefitters, and reinforcing practical knowledge with Plumbing Basics for Contractors can help build a more organized study routine.

Additional review with the International Fuel Gas Code and OSHA construction regulations can strengthen preparation in fuel gas and safety. The goal is to help candidates develop greater familiarity with the subjects, improve reference-navigation efficiency, and approach exam day with a practical study strategy.

FAQ Section

How many questions are on the Tennessee Limited Licensed Plumber exam?

The current Prov LLP examination contains 40 questions.

How much time is allowed for the Tennessee LLP exam?

Candidates currently receive 2 hours to complete the 40-question examination.

Is the Tennessee Limited Licensed Plumber exam open book?

Yes. The Tennessee LLP examination is open book, subject to Prov's rules for authorized reference materials.

Which references are currently listed by Prov for the LLP exam?

Prov's current primary LLP reference list identifies the International Plumbing Code, 2021; Mathematics for Plumbers and Pipefitters, 8th Edition; and Plumbing Basics for Contractors, 4th Edition, 2021.

The current LLP examination includes OSHA Safety questions. The OSHA construction regulations provide additional safety material relevant to plumbing and construction workplaces.

What is the largest subject area on the Tennessee LLP exam?

Drain, Waste, and Vent Systems is currently the largest category with 10 questions. Isometrics is the second-largest with 7 questions.

What type of work does the Tennessee LLP license cover?

The LLP license applies to qualifying plumbing work costing less than $25,000 per project in municipalities using the Tennessee Division of Fire Prevention for permits or inspections.

Are local plumbing requirements still important after receiving an LLP license?

Yes. Local jurisdictions may have additional licensing, permit, inspection, or code requirements. Plumbers should check the requirements where they intend to perform work.

No. Passing the examination is part of the state LLP licensing process, and local licensing, permitting, inspection, and scope requirements may also apply.

Study according to the current LLP exam categories and practice using the references under timed conditions. Focus heavily on drain, waste and vent systems, isometrics, plumbing-code navigation, water distribution, fuel gas, and plumbing mathematics while still reviewing every subject on the exam outline.

Candidates should understand requirements related to fixture installation, fixture fittings, minimum required fixtures, clearances, approved materials, connections, and inspection considerations. Fixture questions may require candidates to identify proper installation requirements or determine whether a described condition meets the code.

Water heaters are another major topic. Candidates should review provisions related to installation, location, access, safety devices, temperature and pressure relief, discharge piping, protection, and related inspection requirements. Water heater questions often require careful reading because small details in the question can affect the correct answer.

Water supply and distribution should be studied carefully. Candidates should become familiar with pipe materials, sizing concepts, pressure requirements, protection from contamination, valves, supports, joints, and installation requirements. Inspection questions may involve determining whether a water distribution system is properly installed, protected, tested, or supported.

Sanitary drainage is a core P1 topic. Candidates should review drainage pipe sizing, slope, cleanouts, fixture connections, fittings, materials, joints, and installation rules. Drainage questions may require table use or careful application of minimum slope and sizing requirements. Students should practice reading tables and checking notes because drainage provisions often depend on exact conditions.

Venting is one of the most important areas for residential plumbing inspector preparation. Candidates should review vent types, vent sizing, vent connections, vent termination, wet venting, common venting concepts, and minimum installation requirements. Venting questions can be challenging because candidates must understand both the purpose of the vent and the code rules that govern its installation.

Traps and cleanouts should also be reviewed in detail. Candidates should understand trap requirements, trap seals, prohibited traps, cleanout access, cleanout locations, and inspection expectations. These topics frequently appear in residential plumbing inspection because they affect system function, maintenance access, and health protection.

Materials, joints, connections, grades, pipe support, and testing are also important. Candidates should know how to locate approved materials, determine proper joining methods, check support spacing, review required tests, and identify installation conditions that may damage building components or compromise system performance.

The W25 Missouri (Springfield) Journeyman Plumber exam is a 70-question, multiple-choice exam with a 3-hour time limit. The listed reference for this exam is the 2018 International Plumbing Code.

To stay on pace, treat the exam like a job-site call: read carefully, identify what the question is really asking, and go straight to the code section that controls the answer. Many candidates lose time by searching broadly. Strong candidates use the IPC structure—definitions, scoping language, tables, and exceptions—to confirm the correct choice quickly.

Major content areas for the W25 Journeyman Plumber exam are weighted toward practical code use. Expect your study time to pay off most when you focus on:

  • Administration / General Regulations (40%) – installation requirements, definitions/terms, testing, and materials
  • Plumbing Fixtures (17%) – including water heaters, water closets and urinals, and specialty fixtures
  • Water Supply and Distribution (14%) – distribution/piping, pressure, and potable water protection
  • Sanitary Drainage (13%) – building drainage, sumps/ejectors, indirect and special waste systems
  • Plumbing Vent Requirements (7%) – vent connections/grades and vent terminals
  • Traps, Interceptors, and Separators (7%) – installation and application requirements
  • Storm Drainage (2%)

That breakdown is useful for planning your prep: hit the bigger sections first, then tighten up your accuracy on the smaller categories. A smart approach is to study by “navigation sets”—learn how the IPC organizes each system, then practice finding answers until it becomes routine.

Open Book Test

The Springfield, Missouri W25 Journeyman Plumber exam is an open book exam. Open book doesn’t mean easy—it means the exam rewards candidates who can locate code answers efficiently. The clock moves fast, and you won’t have time to look up everything. The goal is to be familiar enough with the IPC that you can confirm details quickly while relying on your baseline trade knowledge for straightforward items.

To prepare for an open book code exam, build these habits early:

  • Learn the IPC layout (chapter themes, where key systems live, how definitions and exceptions work).
  • Practice with realistic timing so you can answer and move on without second-guessing.
  • Use the index strategically—then confirm by reading the controlling section language.
  • Watch for exceptions and table notes, which often separate a correct answer from a close distractor.

Licensing Steps

For Springfield, Missouri contractor/trades testing, the licensing process begins with the local jurisdiction. Before you can schedule the ICC/Pearson VUE examination, you must submit a license application to the local licensing agency (Building Development Services). After you receive approval/notification from the licensing agency, you may apply for and schedule your exam.

Once approved, you schedule your exam through Pearson VUE under the ICC contractor/trades program. After you test, electronic exam results are typically available immediately upon completion at the test center. If you do not pass, ICC policy requires waiting 10 days before retaking a failed exam—use that window to tighten up code navigation and the sections where you lost time.

If you have questions about which exam you need for your role or certification level, the local jurisdiction is the final authority on which exam(s) apply to your situation. Your best move is to confirm your trade category and required exam code (W25_MO_S) before scheduling.

Test Information and Study Materials

This exam is multiple-choice and designed to measure how well you apply code concepts—not just whether you can memorize a rule. The most effective study strategy is to combine code reading with targeted practice:

  • Start with the big-weight sections: Administration/General Regulations and Plumbing Fixtures. Build comfort with common terms, installation requirements, and where the IPC places key requirements.
  • Create a navigation routine: When you miss a question in practice, don’t just note the right answer—write down the exact IPC section and what clue in the question should have sent you there.
  • Practice “two-step confirmation”: (1) locate the likely section quickly, then (2) confirm by reading the controlling sentence, exception, or table note.
  • Train your timing: The exam is 70 questions in 3 hours. Practice answering with a steady pace, leaving time to review flagged questions at the end.

When you study the IPC, focus on how code writers communicate requirements. Words like “shall,” “shall not,” “exception,” “where,” “listed,” and “approved” matter. Getting comfortable with that language helps you avoid common multiple-choice traps that feel right in the field but don’t match the written code requirement.

1) Build a weekly topic rhythm. Instead of trying to study everything at once, rotate through major areas and revisit them through spaced review:

  • IPC code navigation: definitions, system expectations, and locating requirements quickly.
  • IFGC safety logic: hazard awareness and recognizing conditions that change outcomes.
  • Trade math routines: units, conversions, clean setup, and accuracy checks.
  • OSHA jobsite safety: scenario-based hazard recognition and responsibility.

2) Treat code study as jobsite decision-making. Code becomes easier when you connect it to outcomes. As you review a requirement, ask:

  • What jobsite decision does this guide?
  • What mistake would violate it?
  • What safety, health, or performance outcome is it protecting?

This approach helps your brain store “why it matters,” which improves retention and speeds up decision-making under exam conditions.

3) Use a “right book first” habit. Many candidates lose time because they start searching before choosing the correct reference. Train a simple rule:

  • IPC first for plumbing system requirements and installation expectations.
  • IFGC first for fuel gas safety logic and fuel gas installation reasoning.
  • Math reference first when the question is clearly calculation-driven or conversion-driven.
  • OSHA first when the question describes a jobsite condition, hazard, or safety responsibility.

When you choose the correct book first, your tabs and highlights do their job: they help you confirm faster.

4) Study fuel gas as “hazard-control thinking.” IFGC study is strongest when you connect requirements to what they prevent. Train a habit of asking:

  • What hazard does this reduce?
  • What installation choice does it influence?
  • What could go wrong if this is ignored?

When you learn the “why,” scenario questions become easier because you’re reasoning from safety intent instead of hunting for a line of text.

  • Write givens clearly and label units.
  • Identify what the question is asking (units and final form).
  • Use consistent conversions (don’t improvise).
  • Check reasonableness before moving on.

6) Practice open-book navigation on purpose. Highlighting and tabs help most when you also train a consistent method:

  • Identify the topic first (IPC vs IFGC vs math vs OSHA).
  • Go to the best reference first (don’t search the wrong book).
  • Confirm the key condition that changes the outcome.
  • Answer and move on without over-searching.

7) Use active recall to make information stick. After each study session:

  • Write a short summary from memory.
  • Explain the concept out loud as if teaching it to a newer apprentice.
  • Create quick “why it matters” notes tied to real outcomes.

8) Make OSHA study scenario-based. OSHA content is easier to retain through jobsite situations: ladder use, fall protection scenarios, PPE decisions, housekeeping, tool hazards, and hazard recognition. Scenario-based review helps you apply safety concepts more confidently when questions describe a worksite condition.

9) Use spaced review to keep retention high. Short, consistent sessions repeated weekly usually outperform occasional marathon study days. Spaced review is how your study becomes dependable under exam pressure.

Exam Details

The Delaware Master Plumber examination evaluates the knowledge needed to provide plumbing services involving the design, installation, construction, replacement, service, repair, alteration, and modification of piping, fixtures, and related equipment used to bring water into a building and remove liquid and water-carried waste. The authorized plumbing scope also includes the installation and connection of gas piping.

The examination contains 100 questions and allows three hours for completion. The published subject areas include:

  • General Knowledge: 16 questions
  • Isometrics and Plan Reading: 8 questions
  • Plumbing Math: 8 questions
  • Drain, Waste, and Vent Systems: 14 questions
  • Water Supply and Distribution: 14 questions
  • Fixtures and Fittings: 8 questions
  • Water Heaters: 10 questions
  • Fuel Gas Systems: 10 questions
  • Storm and Roof Drainage: 6 questions
  • Safety: 6 questions

General knowledge questions may involve plumbing terminology, approved materials, fittings, tools, installation methods, testing procedures, inspections, system components, and standard trade practices. Candidates should understand how individual components contribute to the performance and safety of the complete plumbing system.

Isometric and plan-reading questions may require candidates to interpret symbols, dimensions, elevations, fixture locations, piping routes, branches, stacks, vents, developed lengths, and system layouts. Candidates should practice translating a drawing into the information needed for code application, sizing, or calculation.

Plumbing mathematics may involve measurements, areas, volumes, slopes, offsets, developed lengths, pressure, flow, fixture units, pipe sizing, and other trade calculations. Candidates should practice organizing the information provided, selecting the correct method, tracking units, and confirming that the final result is reasonable.

Drain, waste, and vent preparation should include drainage materials, horizontal and vertical piping, fixture connections, traps, cleanouts, slope, drainage sizing, venting methods, and installation requirements. Candidates should understand how proper drainage and venting support flow while protecting fixture trap seals.

Water-supply and distribution questions may address approved materials, service piping, distribution systems, valves, pressure control, backflow protection, sizing, fixture demand, water hammer, and installation practices. Candidates should become comfortable using code tables and applying the conditions and limitations connected with each table.

Fixtures and fittings questions may involve installation, spacing, clearances, connections, materials, traps, faucets, and required components. Water-heater preparation should include equipment installation, temperature and pressure relief, drainage, combustion considerations, safety, and system protection.

Fuel gas questions may involve piping materials, system sizing, valves, regulators, appliance connections, testing, combustion air, venting, and safe installation practices. Storm and roof drainage questions may address roof areas, drains, conductors, leaders, piping sizes, and storm-water disposal.

Open Book Test

The Delaware Master Plumber examination is an open-book, timed test. Candidates may use authorized references while following the testing provider’s current rules for approved titles, editions, permanent tabs, highlighting, notes, inserts, calculators, and other materials.

An open-book format does not eliminate the need for thorough preparation. Candidates must complete 100 questions within three hours, leaving limited time for long searches. Strong preparation combines plumbing knowledge with the ability to identify the correct reference and locate the applicable section efficiently.

The books in this package are highlighted and tabbed to support that process. Tabs provide convenient starting points for major chapters and common exam subjects, while highlighting identifies useful definitions, tables, technical explanations, code requirements, calculations, and system concepts.

The International Plumbing Code, 2018 supports questions involving fixtures, water supply, sanitary drainage, traps, vents, water heaters, storm drainage, materials, testing, and plumbing-system installation requirements.

The International Fuel Gas Code, 2018 supports preparation involving fuel gas piping materials, system sizing, valves, regulators, appliance connections, combustion air, venting, pressure testing, and related installation requirements.

Plumbing Basics for Contractors, 3rd Edition, 2014 supports review of plumbing mathematics, plan reading, isometric drawings, materials, fixtures, drainage, venting, water distribution, system principles, and general trade knowledge.

Develop a consistent search method during preparation. Begin by identifying the main subject and important terms in the question. Choose the reference most likely to contain the answer, use the index or table of contents, and read the complete applicable section.

When using a table, review its title, headings, notes, and limitations. The correct answer may depend on developed length, pipe material, pressure, slope, fixture load, building conditions, or another factor described in the question.

Do not rely only on one highlighted sentence or table entry. Read nearby definitions, exceptions, notes, diagrams, and related provisions because an additional condition may change which requirement applies.

Candidates should review the current examination instructions before test day and confirm that their books and book preparation comply with the rules for the scheduled examination.

Licensing Steps

The Delaware Board of Plumbing, Heating, Ventilation, Air Conditioning and Refrigeration Examiners regulates Master Plumber licenses. Applicants must complete the Delaware professional licensing process and receive Board approval before taking the Master Plumber examination.

  1. Create or access a DELPROS account. Delaware professional license applications are submitted through the state’s online licensing system.
  2. Complete the Master Plumber application. Provide the requested personal, apprenticeship, employment, experience, examination, and licensing information.
  3. Arrange for license verification. Verification may be required from jurisdictions where the applicant currently holds or previously held a professional license.
  4. Document plumbing experience. Submit employment verification and supporting records for the licensing pathway under which the application is filed.
  5. Provide apprenticeship documentation when applicable. Applicants using the journeyperson pathway must submit the required apprenticeship completion records.
  6. Complete the apprenticeship bypass requirement when applicable. Applicants without a qualifying journeyperson certificate must receive approval and complete the required bypass examination process.

For general plumbing, candidates should review water piping principles, plumbing code organization, valves, fittings, system connections, protection of piping, installation requirements, and plumbing terminology. Since the CR-78 classification connects solar equipment to existing plumbing stub-outs at the water tank location, plumbing code familiarity is a major part of preparation.

For pipes and materials, candidates should study material selection, pipe compatibility, temperature considerations, pressure-related concepts, joining methods, supports, fittings, and installation practices. Solar liquid systems rely on properly selected and installed piping components to move heated liquid through the system safely and effectively.

For open and closed loop systems, candidates should understand how direct open loop, indirect closed loop, and thermosyphon systems operate. Study should include system circulation, heat transfer, water movement, use of heat exchangers, system protection, and the differences between direct and indirect heating arrangements.

For pumps and storage systems, candidates should review pump purpose, circulation, storage tanks, expansion tanks, heat exchangers, flow, controls, and component relationships. These topics are central to solar water heating and solar pool heating system performance.

For system designs, candidates should study how the complete system is arranged, how collectors connect to piping and storage, how pumps and controls interact, and how the system ties into existing plumbing. This section has 12 questions and should receive careful attention during exam preparation.

For collectors, candidates should review collector function, liquid flow through collectors, placement considerations, solar heating principles, and system integration. For controls, candidates should study sensors, low voltage controls, control sequence, pump activation, and the way control components support safe and efficient operation.

For safety, candidates should review OSHA construction standards and understand how jobsite safety applies to solar plumbing work. Candidates may need to understand ladder safety, fall hazards, personal protective equipment, electrical awareness, tools, equipment, and general construction-site hazard prevention.

A strong study routine combines reading, reference navigation, and timed practice. Candidates should learn where major topics are located in each book, mark permitted sections before the exam, and practice finding information quickly. FAQ Section

What is the Arizona CR-78 contractor license for?

The Arizona CR-78 Solar Plumbing, Liquid Systems Only Residential / Commercial Contractor classification covers installation, alteration, and repair of solar water heating systems operating at temperatures not exceeding 220 degrees Fahrenheit, including thermosyphon, direct open loop, and indirect closed loop systems. It also includes certain solar pool heating systems and related solar plumbing components.

Is the Arizona CR-78 exam open book?

Yes. The Arizona CR-78 exam allows specific approved reference materials in the examination center. Candidates must bring their own approved books and follow the testing rules for markings, tabs, binding, and loose materials.

How many questions are on the Arizona CR-78 exam?

The Arizona CR-78 Solar Plumbing, Liquid Systems Only Residential / Commercial Contractor exam has 60 questions.

How much time is allowed for the Arizona CR-78 exam?

The time allowed for the Arizona CR-78 exam is 150 minutes.

What score is required to pass the Arizona CR-78 exam?

The minimum passing score for the Arizona CR-78 exam is 70%.

What topics are covered on the Arizona CR-78 exam?

The exam covers general plumbing, pipes and materials, open and closed loop systems, pumps and storage systems, system designs, collectors, and controls.

Which books are allowed into the Arizona CR-78 exam?

The allowed books include Code of Federal Regulations - 29 CFR Part 1926 (OSHA), International Plumbing Code, 2018, and International Mechanical Code, 2018.

Can I highlight or underline my books before the exam?

Yes. Approved reference materials may be highlighted, underlined, annotated, and indexed before the examination session. Candidates may not write, highlight, underline, or index the books during the exam.

Are removable tabs allowed in the exam books?

No. Temporary removable tabs are not allowed. References may be tabbed or indexed with permanent tabs only.

Can I bring loose notes into the exam?

No. Additional loose or attached papers are not permitted with approved references.

Can downloaded references be used in the testing center?

Downloaded references may be used when they are bound. A downloaded reference may be spiral bound or hole-punched and placed in a binder.

Does the CR-78 classification include air as a transfer medium?

No. The CR-78 classification is for solar plumbing liquid systems only and excludes air as a transfer medium.

Why should I study with the exam-room approved books?

Studying with the approved books helps candidates become familiar with the same references they can use during the exam. This supports faster lookup, better organization, and stronger preparation for open book questions.

A strong Nevada C-1 study plan should organize the exam into systems and connect each system with its most relevant reference.

Drain, Waste, and Vent Systems should receive substantial attention because this is the largest individual category. Candidates should review drainage sizing, slope, vents, fixture units, cleanouts, traps, interceptors, and sanitary plumbing requirements using the Uniform Plumbing Code.

Water Supply should include sizing, pressure, materials, valves, distribution, backflow protection, supports, and system protection. Practice using UPC tables and locating applicable requirements quickly.

Gas Systems should be studied with NFPA 54 and NFPA 58 nearby. Candidates should understand the difference between natural gas and LP-Gas systems and know which code applies to each.

Fire Sprinklers should be reviewed with NFPA 13. Candidates should become familiar with sprinkler system components, piping, installation concepts, and the organization of the standard.

Hydronics, Boilers, and Chilled Water Piping should be studied with the Uniform Mechanical Code. Review piping systems, valves, controls, pumps, equipment, supports, heat transfer, and system operation.

Water Heaters and Venting should include installation, combustion air, venting, temperature and pressure protection, fuel-gas considerations, and related code provisions.

Traps and Interceptors account for 8 questions. Candidates should understand trap function, seal protection, interceptor applications, installation requirements, and related UPC provisions.

Plumbing Mathematics and Isometric Analysis also account for 8 questions. Candidates should practice measurements, pipe calculations, elevations, areas, volumes, offsets, and interpretation of piping layouts.

Code books can provide tables and values, but candidates should still be comfortable performing the calculations. Efficient mathematics can save time that can then be used for more difficult reference lookups.

Storm Drainage should include roof drainage, conductors, sizing, drainage pathways, and related code requirements.

Definitions should also be reviewed because technical terminology can affect the meaning of a question. Understanding how a code defines a term can help candidates interpret both the question and the applicable requirement.

Exam Details

The Arizona Plumbing, Residential Contractor (R-37R) trade examination evaluates knowledge associated with residential plumbing work and related systems. The exam may require candidates to apply code provisions, interpret technical requirements, use tables, recognize installation methods, and identify safe construction practices.

Plumbing subjects can include drainage, waste and vent systems, water distribution, backflow prevention, plumbing fixtures, traps, interceptors, water heaters, storm drainage, indirect waste, materials, testing, and general installation requirements. Candidates may also need to interpret piping layouts and determine how code provisions apply to residential conditions.

Fuel gas questions may involve pipe sizing, appliance connections, shutoff valves, regulators, combustion air, venting, testing, and installation requirements. Mechanical questions may involve ventilation, exhaust systems, equipment, combustion air, appliances, and related mechanical installations.

Fire sprinkler preparation requires candidates to understand the different applications of NFPA 13, NFPA 13D, and NFPA 13R. Each standard addresses a different type of sprinkler-system application or occupancy condition. Identifying the correct standard is an important first step when answering a sprinkler question.

Construction-safety questions may come from 29 CFR Part 1926. Candidates should be prepared to review excavation, ladders, scaffolds, personal protective equipment, fall protection, electrical hazards, material handling, and other jobsite requirements.

The Arizona onsite wastewater reference supports questions involving state provisions for onsite wastewater treatment facilities. Candidates should become familiar with the terminology, organization, and regulatory structure used in this publication.

Questions may ask a candidate to identify the correct code section, choose an approved material, apply a sizing table, interpret a definition, recognize an unsafe condition, or determine which standard governs the situation described. Preparation should therefore combine trade knowledge with reference-book navigation.

Open Book Test

The Arizona R-37R trade examination is an open-book test. Candidates may use approved reference materials during the examination, subject to the current testing provider’s rules for permitted books and book preparation.

Open-book testing does not eliminate the need to study. The exam library includes multiple detailed codes and technical standards, and searching every book for every answer can consume valuable time. Candidates should learn the purpose of each reference before attempting timed practice.

A practical navigation process begins by identifying the subject of the question. A sanitary drainage question will usually lead to the International Plumbing Code. A fuel gas sizing question will likely require the International Fuel Gas Code. A mechanical ventilation question may belong in the International Mechanical Code, while a residential sprinkler question may require NFPA 13D or NFPA 13R.

After selecting the book, candidates should use the table of contents or index to locate the most relevant chapter or term. Reading the surrounding section is important because exceptions, notes, definitions, and table headings may change how a requirement applies.

Regular practice with the actual exam books can help candidates recognize chapter layouts and useful index terms. Candidates should also practice using tables, diagrams, cross-references, and appendices rather than relying only on highlighted passages or memorized page numbers.

Licensing Steps

Begin by confirming that the R-37R residential plumbing classification matches the work the applicant or business plans to perform. Arizona offers residential, commercial, and dual contractor classifications, and the selected classification should correspond with the intended scope of work.

Identify the qualifying party for the contractor license. The qualifying party is the individual responsible for meeting the applicable experience, knowledge, and examination requirements connected with the requested classification.

Complete the required R-37R trade examination unless an authorized waiver applies. A separate Arizona statutes and rules requirement may also apply as part of the contractor licensing process.

Complete the required background-check process and gather the documents associated with the selected business structure. Arizona contractor licenses may be issued to eligible business entities such as sole proprietorships, partnerships, limited liability companies, and corporations.

Obtain the required contractor bond and prepare the supporting application records. These may include identification, business formation documents, qualifying-party information, examination results, experience documentation, background-check records, bond information, and signed application forms.

Submit the completed application to the Arizona Registrar of Contractors. The agency reviews the materials and determines whether the applicant has met the requirements for the requested license classification.

Passing the trade exam does not automatically issue a contractor license. The applicant must complete the full licensing process and receive approval before performing work that requires the license.

State Requirements

Arizona contractor licensing is administered by the Arizona Registrar of Contractors. Applicants must satisfy the requirements associated with the requested classification, qualifying party, examinations or authorized waivers, experience, background checks, contractor bonding, business records, and application documentation.

The R-37R classification applies to residential plumbing contracting within the scope assigned to that classification. Candidates should not assume that a residential classification automatically authorizes commercial plumbing work or activities outside the defined scope.

The qualifying party should have experience related to the work covered by the requested license. Applicants should maintain records describing employment, project responsibilities, supervisory duties, and hands-on plumbing experience.

Business names, ownership information, and qualifying-party details should remain consistent across formation documents, identification, background-check records, bond paperwork, and the contractor license application. Inconsistent information may lead to requests for corrections or additional documentation.

Applicants should use the current forms and instructions issued for their application cycle. Examination procedures, administrative forms, and licensing requirements may be updated.

Oklahoma Plumbing and Natural Gas Contractor Exam Prep - Live Virtual + Self Study Training

Prepare for the Oklahoma Plumbing and Natural Gas Contractor licensing examinations with a structured combination of live virtual instruction and self-study training. This program is designed for plumbing professionals pursuing Oklahoma contractor licensing who want organized preparation for technical plumbing systems, natural gas piping, trade mathematics, OSHA construction safety, open-book reference navigation, and contractor Business and Law topics.

The Oklahoma Plumbing Contractor license is regulated by the Oklahoma Construction Industries Board. Candidates pursuing the contractor classification need to demonstrate practical plumbing knowledge while also preparing for the business, legal, and regulatory responsibilities associated with operating a plumbing contracting business.

The technical examination covers plumbing systems including sanitary drainage, waste and vent systems, water supply, fixtures, piping, valves, natural gas systems, appliances, vents, flues, tanks, isometric drawings, calculations, and construction safety. Candidates should be prepared to combine trade knowledge with code navigation and mathematical problem solving.

Live Virtual + Self Study Training gives candidates two complementary ways to prepare. Live virtual instruction helps organize the examination into focused subjects, while self-study allows students to spend additional time practicing code navigation, plumbing mathematics, pipe sizing, venting, drainage, gas systems, isometric analysis, safety, and contractor Business and Law.

The program is organized around the International Plumbing Code, 2024; International Fuel Gas Code, 2024; Mathematics for Plumbers and Pipefitters, 8th Edition; and Code of Federal Regulations - 29 CFR Part 1926 (OSHA). Contractor Business and Law preparation uses the listed Oklahoma statutes, administrative regulations, lien law, and NASCLA contractor business reference.

Exam Details

The Oklahoma Plumbing Contractor and Natural Gas examination is administered through PSI after the Oklahoma Construction Industries Board determines that an applicant meets the applicable licensing qualifications and is eligible to proceed with testing.

  • Exam: Oklahoma Plumbing Contractor and Natural Gas
  • Number of Questions: 85 scored questions
  • Passing Score: 75%
  • Passing Raw Score: 64 correct answers
  • Time Allowed: 180 minutes
  • Testing Provider: PSI

The technical examination is divided into the following major subject areas:

  • General Plumbing Knowledge and Regulations: 10 questions
  • Piping, Valves, and Control Valves: 8 questions
  • Fixtures and Equipment: 8 questions
  • Water Supply: 10 questions
  • Drains and Sewers: 10 questions
  • Vents: 13 questions
  • Traps, Interceptors, Indirect, and Special Waste: 5 questions
  • Isometric Analysis: 7 questions
  • Fuel Gas: 10 questions
  • Safety: 4 questions

Vents is the largest individual examination category with 13 questions. Candidates should understand vent installation, developed length, sizing, connections, and the relationship between vent systems and sanitary drainage.

General Plumbing Knowledge and Regulations contains 10 questions. Preparation should include head pressure, pipe joints, solvent-welded joints, calculations of area and volume, water-supply friction loss, permits and inspections, job costs, structural penetrations, fire integrity, pipe offsets, trenching, excavation, backfill, and fitting identification.

Water Supply contains 10 questions involving water distribution lines, protection of potable water supplies, and backflow. Drains and Sewers contains another 10 questions addressing drain and sewer piping, building sewers, cleanouts, sewage ejectors and sump pumps, drain and waste piping, and storm drainage.

Fuel Gas contains 10 questions and is a significant part of this contractor examination. Study should include gas distribution pipe sizing, regulators, hangers and supports, changes in direction, concealed piping, joints and connections, valves, outlets, drip legs and sediment traps, appliances, combustion air, chimneys and vents, outdoor gas piping, testing, inspection, and piping material requirements.

Isometric Analysis contains seven questions. Candidates should practice reading plumbing isometric drawings and identifying how fixtures, drainage, venting, and piping arrangements relate to code and sizing requirements.

Safety contains four questions covering construction jobsite responsibilities such as personal protective equipment, excavation safety, trench protection, ventilation, first aid, signs and barricades, tools, ladders, scaffolds, hazardous materials, material handling, and fall protection.

Contractor candidates also prepare for the separate Oklahoma Plumbing Business and Law examination.

  • Plumbing Business and Law Questions: 50 scored questions
  • Passing Score: 75%
  • Passing Raw Score: 37 correct answers
  • Time Allowed: 120 minutes

Business and Law preparation includes bidding and estimating, project management and supervision, contracts, financial management, labor and personnel, risk management, insurance, bonds, payroll, payroll taxes, liens, and Oklahoma plumbing licensing requirements.

Open Book Test

The Oklahoma Plumbing Contractor and Natural Gas technical examination is an open-book test. Candidates are responsible for bringing permitted references into the testing center and following the applicable examination rules for those materials.

The technical examination reference list includes the International Plumbing Code, 2024 edition with Oklahoma revisions; International Fuel Gas Code, 2024 edition with Oklahoma revisions; Mathematics for Plumbers and Pipefitters, 8th Edition; and Code of Federal Regulations - 29 CFR Part 1926 (OSHA) with applicable amendments.

Approved reference materials may be highlighted, underlined, and indexed before testing. Permanent tabs may be used. Temporary tabs such as Post-it notes are not permitted. Candidates should organize and practice with their references before examination day.

The International Plumbing Code should be used for plumbing-system preparation involving fixtures, water supply, drainage, vents, traps, piping, and related code requirements. Candidates should learn the organization of the code and become comfortable using the index, chapter structure, definitions, tables, and cross-references.

The International Fuel Gas Code should be used for gas piping, regulators, sizing, joints, valves, outlets, appliance-related requirements, combustion air, venting, testing, and inspection. Candidates should practice identifying gas-system questions quickly so they can move directly to the appropriate reference.

Mathematics for Plumbers and Pipefitters supports trade calculations involving measurements, area, volume, pipe offsets, and other mathematical applications. Repeated calculation practice is important because mathematical questions can consume valuable exam time if the candidate is unfamiliar with the process.

Code of Federal Regulations - 29 CFR Part 1926 supports construction-safety preparation. Candidates should become familiar with how the OSHA reference is organized and know where major safety subjects can be located.

Licensing Steps

The Oklahoma Construction Industries Board regulates plumbing contractor licensing. Contractor applicants must satisfy applicable experience requirements before proceeding through the application and examination process.

  1. Gain qualifying plumbing trade experience. Build verifiable experience while working within Oklahoma's plumbing licensing and supervision structure.
  2. Maintain apprentice registration when applicable. Oklahoma plumbing experience used toward licensing qualifications must be properly documented through apprentice registration unless the experience was lawfully obtained under an applicable exemption.
  3. Meet journeyman-level qualifications. Contractor applicants must satisfy the applicable requirements established for Oklahoma plumbing journeyman licensing.
  4. Gain additional contractor-level experience. Plumbing contractor applicants must meet the journeyman requirements plus an additional year of qualifying plumbing trade experience.
  5. Submit the plumbing contractor application. Provide the Oklahoma Construction Industries Board with the required application and supporting experience documentation.
  6. Receive examination authorization. The applicant's qualifications are reviewed before testing authorization is provided.
  7. Schedule the required examinations. Approved candidates arrange testing through PSI.
  8. Prepare for Plumbing Contractor and Natural Gas. Study plumbing systems, fuel gas, mathematics, isometric analysis, safety, and reference navigation.
  9. Prepare for Plumbing Business and Law. Review Oklahoma plumbing licensing law, regulations, lien law, estimating, contracts, project management, finances, and contractor responsibilities.
  10. Complete the required examinations. Achieve the applicable passing scores required for contractor licensing.
  11. Complete active contractor requirements. Address applicable bond, commercial general liability insurance, and other requirements associated with active contractor status.

State Requirements

Applicants for an Oklahoma plumbing contractor license must be at least 18 years old. Contractor applicants must meet the same basic qualifications as a plumbing journeyman and have an additional year of qualifying plumbing trade experience.

One standard journeyman pathway requires three years of experience in the plumbing trade while employed by a licensed plumbing contractor. Equivalent verifiable plumbing experience gained through qualifying United States military service may also be considered.

Applicants holding a current and good-standing out-of-state plumbing license may also qualify when the license and supporting experience meet Oklahoma requirements.

Approved plumbing education may substitute for part of the required trade experience. Candidates using education toward the qualification requirement should maintain appropriate documentation showing completion of the approved classroom program.

Oklahoma plumbing experience used toward licensing generally must be verifiable through apprentice registration unless the work was lawfully performed under an applicable exemption. Candidates should maintain organized records of employment, apprenticeship, education, and trade experience.

Contractor licensing extends beyond passing examinations. Active plumbing contractors must satisfy applicable bond and commercial general liability insurance requirements and maintain their licensing status in accordance with Oklahoma requirements.

Reference Books

  • International Plumbing Code, 2024
    This approved technical reference supports preparation for plumbing fixtures, water supply, sanitary drainage, vents, traps, piping, indirect waste, storm drainage, and related plumbing requirements. Candidates should prepare using the 2024 edition with applicable Oklahoma revisions.
  • International Fuel Gas Code, 2024
    This approved technical reference supports study of gas piping, sizing, regulators, supports, joints, valves, outlets, appliances, combustion air, chimneys, vents, testing, inspection, and fuel-gas installation requirements. Preparation should include the applicable Oklahoma revisions.
  • Mathematics for Plumbers and Pipefitters, 8th Edition
    This approved technical reference supports plumbing mathematics involving measurements, area, volume, piping calculations, pipe offsets, and other mathematical applications relevant to plumbing and pipefitting work.
  • Code of Federal Regulations - 29 CFR Part 1926 (OSHA)
    This approved construction-safety reference supports preparation for excavation, trench safety, personal protective equipment, ladders, scaffolds, fall protection, ventilation, hazardous materials, tools, material handling, and related jobsite safety requirements.
  • Oklahoma Plumbing License Law of 1955, Oklahoma Statutes, Title 59, Chapter 27
    This statutory reference supports contractor Business and Law study involving Oklahoma plumbing licensing authority, regulated plumbing work, license requirements, and contractor responsibilities.
  • Oklahoma Plumbing Industry Regulations, Oklahoma Administrative Code, Title 158, Chapter 30
    This administrative reference supports preparation involving Oklahoma plumbing classifications, apprentices, journeymen, contractors, experience requirements, licensing responsibilities, and industry regulation.
  • Oklahoma Fine Schedule of the Construction Industries Board, Oklahoma Administrative Code, Title 158, Chapter 10
    This reference supports contractor preparation involving Oklahoma Construction Industries Board compliance and enforcement topics.
  • Oklahoma Lien Law, Oklahoma Statutes, Title 42, Chapter 3
    This statutory material supports contractor Business and Law preparation involving construction liens and payment-related rights and responsibilities.
  • NASCLA Contractors Guide to Business, Law and Project Management, 14th Edition
    This contractor business reference supports preparation for estimating, bidding, project management, contracts, financial management, personnel, insurance, bonds, risk management, and other business responsibilities.

Test Information and Study Materials

A productive Oklahoma Plumbing and Natural Gas Contractor study plan should divide preparation into plumbing code, fuel gas, mathematics, isometric analysis, OSHA safety, reference navigation, and Business and Law.

Prioritize venting. Vents is the largest individual exam category. Review vent installation, developed length, connections, sizing concepts, and how vent systems work with sanitary drainage and plumbing fixtures.

Strengthen water-supply and drainage knowledge. Review water distribution, potable water protection, backflow, sanitary drainage, building sewers, cleanouts, sewage ejectors, sump pumps, waste piping, and storm drainage.

Practice fuel-gas questions. Study gas distribution sizing, regulators, supports, joints, valves, outlets, sediment traps, appliances, combustion air, chimneys, vents, outdoor supply piping, inspections, testing, and materials.

Practice plumbing mathematics. Work through area, volume, friction-loss, pipe-offset, and measurement problems regularly. Develop a consistent method for identifying the values given in a question and selecting the appropriate formula or calculation process.

Work on isometric analysis. Practice interpreting piping drawings and identifying how fixtures, drains, vents, and piping arrangements connect. Use drawing practice to reinforce code navigation and system understanding.

Prepare for OSHA safety. Review excavation, trenching, PPE, ventilation, ladders, scaffolds, fall protection, signs and barricades, tools, hazardous materials, and material handling.

Study Business and Law separately. Use the Oklahoma statutes, administrative regulations, lien law, fine schedule, and NASCLA contractor guide to prepare for estimating, project management, contracts, finances, personnel, risk management, and licensing responsibilities.

The examination assesses knowledge of residential plumbing systems, water distribution, drainage, venting, fuel gas installations, piping materials, plumbing calculations, and construction safety.

  • Exam Name: Residential Contractor Plumbing and Natural Gas.
  • Licensing Authority: Oklahoma Construction Industries Board.

Open Book Test

The Oklahoma Residential Plumbing and Natural Gas Contractor examination is an open book test. Candidates may consult approved technical references during testing under PSI examination rules.

Open-book testing requires an understanding of how plumbing codes and technical references are organized. Candidates must be able to identify the applicable requirements, locate relevant information, and apply that information to practical installation questions.

The examination permits approved reference materials to be highlighted, underlined, and indexed before testing. Permanent reference tabs are permitted, while temporary tabs such as removable sticky notes are prohibited. Handwritten notes and additional loose papers are not allowed.

Students preparing for this examination should practice locating plumbing code provisions, using mathematical formulas, interpreting piping diagrams, and identifying safety requirements.

Important open-book study strategies include:

  • Learning the organization of the 2024 International Residential Code.
  • Reviewing plumbing and fuel gas chapters and technical tables.

  • Locating pipe sizing, installation, and venting requirements.
  • Studying permitted piping materials and joining methods.

During the transition period, candidates may test under the applicable 2018 or 2024 code editions. Beginning December 15, 2026, the examinations use the newly adopted 2024 codes exclusively.

Preparing with the 2024 edition supports familiarity with the updated code requirements associated with Oklahoma's current residential plumbing standards.

Licensing Steps

Obtaining an Oklahoma Residential Plumbing and Natural Gas Contractor license involves meeting the state's qualifications, documenting experience, completing the licensing application, and passing the required examinations.

  1. Identify Your License Classification: Determine whether the Residential Plumbing and Natural Gas Contractor classification matches your professional experience and intended work.
  2. Review Experience Requirements: Evaluate your plumbing employment, journeyman-level experience, and qualifying education against Oklahoma's licensing requirements.
  3. Gather Supporting Documentation: Organize employment records, apprenticeship information, education documents, and other materials required by the Construction Industries Board.
  4. Submit Your Application: Complete the appropriate Oklahoma plumbing contractor licensing application and provide the required documentation.
  5. Receive Examination Approval: The Construction Industries Board evaluates applicant qualifications and determines examination eligibility.
  6. Schedule Your Examinations: After approval, register for the required examinations through PSI.
  7. Prepare for Testing: Study residential plumbing codes, natural gas requirements, mathematics, construction safety, and applicable Business and Law subjects.
  8. Complete the Examinations: Pass the required technical and Business and Law examination components.
  9. Complete License Activation: Fulfill the applicable bonding, insurance, and administrative requirements associated with an active contractor license.

Maintaining organized documentation and a consistent preparation schedule can help candidates manage the licensing process.

Oklahoma State Requirements

Oklahoma regulates plumbing contractor licensing through the Oklahoma Construction Industries Board. Applicants must satisfy qualifying experience requirements and complete the applicable examinations.

Age Requirement: Applicants must be at least 18 years old.

Experience Requirements: Plumbing contractor applicants must satisfy the experience qualifications established for journeyman plumbers, along with one additional year of qualifying plumbing experience.

Journeyman qualification generally requires three years of plumbing trade experience while employed by a licensed plumbing contractor. Qualifying military plumbing experience or an eligible out-of-state plumbing license may also support an application under the state's requirements.

Education Substitutions: Certain approved plumbing education programs may substitute for a portion of the experience requirement. Approved programs containing at least 1,000 classroom hours may qualify for a two-year substitution, while approved programs containing at least 500 classroom hours may qualify for a one-year substitution.

Examination Requirements: Contractor applicants must pass the applicable plumbing trade examination and the required Business and Law examination.

Bonding and Insurance: Oklahoma establishes bonding and insurance requirements for activating a plumbing contractor license, with applicable provisions for qualifying exemptions.

Continuing Education: Licensed plumbing contractors must satisfy Oklahoma's continuing education requirements, including six hours during the applicable 36-month licensing period.

These requirements distinguish contractor licensing from journeyman plumbing qualifications and reflect the additional responsibilities associated with operating a plumbing contracting business.

  • International Residential Code (IRC), 2024

Exam Details

The Mississippi Plumbing Contractor examination is administered through PSI as part of the Mississippi State Board of Contractors licensing process. Before a candidate can schedule the required examination, the contractor license application must first be submitted to the Mississippi State Board of Contractors. After the application is reviewed and the candidate is determined eligible to test, the Board notifies PSI of the candidate's eligibility.

The current Mississippi Plumbing Contractor examination contains 100 questions. Candidates are allowed 300 minutes to complete the examination, and the minimum passing requirement is 73 percent, or 73 correct answers.

The examination content covers a broad range of plumbing knowledge. Current exam topics include general knowledge and mathematics, general plumbing requirements, water supply and distribution, plumbing fixtures and water heaters, drain-waste-and-vent systems, traps, cleanouts and interceptors, isometric analysis, gas appliances and piping, and OSHA safety.

The examination places substantial emphasis on practical plumbing systems and the ability to interpret technical information.
