Candidates should also be prepared to work with mathematical concepts associated with plumbing calculations and field applications.

Safety is another part of the examination. Plumbing contractors work in construction environments where excavation, ladders, tools, personal protective equipment, jobsite hazards, and other OSHA-regulated activities can be relevant. Familiarity with 29 CFR Part 1926 helps candidates prepare for questions involving federal construction safety requirements.

Because the examination covers multiple technical areas, studying only one section of the plumbing code is not an effective preparation strategy. Candidates should build familiarity with the complete range of subjects represented on the test and practice moving between technical references as needed.

Open Book Test

The Mississippi Plumbing Contractor examination is an open-book examination. PSI allows candidates to bring approved reference materials into the examination center under the rules established for the test.

Current PSI rules allow approved references to be highlighted, underlined, and indexed before the examination. References may also be tabbed or indexed using permanent tabs. Temporary tabs, including removable Post-it-style tabs, are not permitted and must be removed before the examination begins.

Candidates are responsible for bringing their own approved reference materials to the examination center. The references are not supplied at the testing location. PSI also prohibits additional loose or attached papers with the approved references, and candidates may not write in their reference books during the examination session.

Open-book testing makes reference-navigation practice particularly important. Candidates should know how to locate subjects through the index, table of contents, chapters, sections, tables, definitions, and permanent tabs. Simply bringing approved books into the exam does not remove the need to understand the material.

The exam is timed, so efficient research matters. When a candidate identifies the subject of a question quickly and knows which reference is most likely to contain the answer, valuable testing time can be preserved. Live instruction and independent reference practice can help develop these navigation habits before exam day.

Licensing Steps

The Mississippi State Board of Contractors regulates contractor licensing in Mississippi. Candidates seeking a Plumbing Contractor classification must complete the licensing process applicable to their business and qualifying party.

  1. Submit the contractor license application. The licensing process begins with an application to the Mississippi State Board of Contractors. Candidates cannot simply register directly for the contractor examination before completing the Board's eligibility process.
  2. Provide the required qualifying-party information. The qualifying party is the individual whose qualifications and examination results support the requested contractor classification.
  3. Submit required supporting documentation. The Board reviews the application and identifies any missing requirements before examination eligibility is issued.
  4. Meet applicable financial requirements. Commercial contractor applicants must satisfy the financial documentation and net-worth requirements applicable to their requested classification.
  5. Receive authorization to test. After the Board determines that the applicant is eligible, MSBOC notifies PSI. PSI then provides the candidate with examination registration information.
  6. Schedule the required examinations. All Mississippi contractor applicants are required to take the Mississippi Law & Business Management examination. A trade examination is also required when applicable to the classification, including the Plumbing Contractor classification.
  7. Prepare for the Plumbing Contractor exam. Study the relevant codes and trade references, practice plumbing calculations and isometric analysis, and become comfortable navigating permitted books.
  8. Take and pass the required examinations. Candidates must meet the minimum passing standard established for each required examination.
  9. Complete any remaining Board requirements. Examination results are one component of the licensing process. The Mississippi State Board of Contractors must approve the complete application before a contractor license is issued.

State Requirements

Mississippi requires applicants to complete the contractor licensing process through the Mississippi State Board of Contractors before operating under a regulated contractor classification. The Board regulates both commercial and residential contractors who bid on or perform covered construction work in Mississippi.

For commercial contractor applications, the qualifying party portion of the application must be completed before the applicant becomes eligible for required examinations. All applicants must take the Mississippi Law & Business Management examination, and applicants must also complete a trade examination when one is required for the requested classification.

Commercial applications also include financial qualification requirements. Applicants must submit a reviewed or audited financial statement prepared and signed by a certified public accountant and completed within the period required by the Board. The financial statement is used as part of the contractor licensing review.

The Board distinguishes between major classifications and other classifications when determining minimum net-worth requirements. Applicants should make sure the requested Plumbing Contractor classification, business structure, qualifying party information, and financial documentation are properly addressed when completing the application.

Passing the Plumbing Contractor examination by itself does not create a Mississippi contractor license. The examination is one part of a broader licensing process that includes Board application review and satisfaction of all requirements applicable to the applicant.

Prepare for the Virginia Master Plumber examination with a combination of live virtual instruction and self-study training designed around the technical plumbing knowledge, Virginia regulations, and reference-navigation skills needed for Master-level preparation. This training option gives candidates the structure of scheduled instruction while allowing additional time between classes to review difficult subjects, practice code navigation, and strengthen their understanding of plumbing systems.

The Virginia Master Plumber examination requires candidates to work with both practical trade knowledge and code-based requirements. Preparation should include drainage, waste and vent systems, water supply systems, backflow prevention, storm drainage, plumbing fixtures, interceptors and traps, general plumbing regulations, and Virginia licensing requirements.

The training is organized around the Virginia Board for Contractors, Individual License and Certification Regulations and the International Plumbing Code, 2021. These references provide the regulatory and technical foundation for focused Virginia Master Plumber exam preparation.

The Virginia regulations address individual tradesman qualifications, standards of practice, standards of conduct, renewal and reinstatement, definitions, and other licensing requirements. The International Plumbing Code provides technical requirements involving plumbing systems, water supply, drainage, venting, fixtures, backflow protection, storm drainage, traps, interceptors, and related installations.

Live virtual training provides scheduled guidance through these subjects, while self-study gives candidates the flexibility to return to important material as often as needed. Candidates can use independent study time to reinforce class topics, work through practice-oriented material, and become more comfortable using the references before exam day.

Live virtual instruction allows candidates to participate in structured exam preparation without attending a physical classroom. Between scheduled sessions, self-study provides additional opportunities to review plumbing code requirements, work with technical tables, revisit difficult concepts, and practice locating information efficiently.

Exam Details

The Virginia Master Plumber credential is an individual tradesman license regulated through the Virginia Board for Contractors. Candidates must satisfy the applicable qualification requirements and receive approval from the Board before taking the examination administered by PSI.

The current Journeyman/Master Plumber examination portion contains 80 items and allows 210 minutes for completion. The current passing score for the Master Plumber examination is 60 correct answers.

The examination content is organized across both Virginia regulatory subjects and technical plumbing topics. The current content outline includes:

  • Standards of Practice: 3 items
  • Standards of Conduct: 2 items
  • Renewal and Reinstatement: 2 items
  • Definitions: 1 item
  • Qualification for Licensure: 1 item
  • Revocation of Licensure: 1 item
  • Drainage Waste and Vents: 24 items
  • Water Supply Systems: 10 items
  • Backflow Prevention: 10 items
  • Storm Drainage Systems: 10 items
  • Plumbing Fixtures: 7 items
  • General Regulations: 5 items
  • Interceptors and Traps: 4 items

The distribution of questions shows why candidates should devote significant study time to drainage, waste and vent systems while still maintaining strong preparation across water supply, backflow prevention, storm drainage, fixtures, traps, and Virginia regulations.

The current Master Tradesman examination fee is $125 and is paid directly to PSI after the candidate has received the required Board approval.

Open Book Test

The Virginia Master Plumber examination is open book. Candidates must bring their own permitted reference materials because the testing site does not provide the books.

The current examination references include the Virginia Board for Contractors, Individual License and Certification Regulations for tradesman regulatory questions and the International Plumbing Code, 2021 for Journeyman and Master Plumber technical questions.

Reference materials may be highlighted, underlined, and indexed before the examination. Permanent tabs are permitted, while removable tabs are not permitted. References containing writing are not allowed, and candidates may not write in their references during the examination session.

An open-book format does not eliminate the need for study. The International Plumbing Code contains extensive technical material, and candidates should not expect to search the entire book for every answer. A stronger approach is to understand the plumbing concept first and use the reference to confirm the applicable requirement.

Live virtual training can help candidates understand where major subjects appear in the references, while self-study provides the repetition needed to make navigation more familiar. Candidates should practice using chapter headings, the index, definitions, tables, and cross-references.

A useful method is to read the question, identify the plumbing subject, select the appropriate reference, locate the applicable section or table, and verify the answer. Repeating that process during preparation helps build a consistent open-book strategy.

Licensing Steps

The Virginia Master Plumber credential is issued to an individual. Candidates must complete the applicable qualification, application, and examination process before licensure.

  1. Review the Master Plumber qualification requirements. Determine which experience or existing-license pathway applies to your background.
  2. Document the required practical experience. Applicants must provide the experience verification required by the Virginia Board for Contractors.
  3. Submit the applicable Tradesman Exam and License Application. The Board reviews the application before granting examination eligibility.
  4. Receive Board approval to test. Pre-approval is required before a candidate may sit for the Virginia Master Plumber examination.
  5. Register and schedule through PSI. After Board approval, candidates may proceed with the examination provider's scheduling process.
  6. Prepare with the applicable references. Study the Virginia regulations and the 2021 International Plumbing Code while practicing technical questions and book navigation.
  7. Complete the Master Plumber examination. Candidates must satisfy the current examination requirement for Master-level licensure.
  8. Complete any remaining licensing requirements. The Board must receive and approve the required licensing information before the individual credential is issued.

Virginia currently provides several qualification pathways for an applicant seeking Master licensure in a trade. An applicant may qualify after holding a valid residential plumber tradesman license for three years, after holding a valid Journeyman license in the trade for at least one year, or by documenting nine years of practical experience in the trade.

State Requirements

The Virginia Board for Contractors regulates individual plumbers through the Tradesmen Program. The Master Plumber credential is an individual license and should be distinguished from a contractor business license.

A person pursuing Master Plumber licensure must satisfy the Board's applicable experience requirements before testing. The Board reviews applications and approves candidates before they may schedule the examination with PSI.

Holding a Master Plumber license does not automatically create a licensed plumbing contracting business. Virginia contractor businesses are licensed separately and must meet the requirements for the appropriate contractor license class and classification or specialty.

For professionals planning to operate through a plumbing contracting company, the Master Plumber credential can be an important individual qualification associated with the business. The company must still complete the separate contractor licensing requirements established by Virginia.

Virginia also regulates continuing education for licensed plumbers as part of the applicable renewal process. Continuing education is separate from initial examination preparation. Exam prep training is intended to help candidates prepare for the Master Plumber examination and does not replace Board-approved continuing education required for license renewal.

Reference Books

  • Virginia Board for Contractors, Individual License and Certification Regulations
    This Virginia regulatory reference addresses individual tradesman licensing and certification requirements. Master Plumber candidates can use it to study standards of practice, standards of conduct, renewal and reinstatement, definitions, qualification requirements, revocation provisions, and other Virginia-specific regulatory material.
  • International Plumbing Code, 2021
    The 2021 International Plumbing Code is the technical code reference used for Journeyman and Master Plumber examination questions. It contains requirements covering drainage, waste and vents, water supply systems, backflow prevention, storm drainage, plumbing fixtures, interceptors, traps, general plumbing requirements, materials, installation, and related technical subjects.

Test Information and Study Materials

The current exam outline makes drainage, waste and vent systems the largest technical study area, with 24 items. Candidates should devote substantial preparation time to drainage piping, sizing, slopes, fittings, cleanouts, vents, vent configurations, trap protection, and related code requirements.

Water supply systems account for 10 items. Candidates should review water-distribution piping, sizing, pressure, valves, materials, connections, system protection, and other requirements contained in the International Plumbing Code. Practice using tables and technical provisions rather than relying only on memorized values.

Backflow prevention also accounts for 10 items. Candidates should understand the purpose of protecting potable-water systems, recognize cross-connection hazards, and become familiar with the code requirements and devices used to prevent contamination or reverse flow.

Storm drainage systems represent another 10 items. Candidates should study roof drainage, conductors, storm piping, sizing, and other provisions governing stormwater removal from buildings.

Plumbing fixtures account for 7 items. Study fixture installation, connections, clearances, required components, fixture fittings, and related provisions. Candidates should know how to use both the code chapters and the index to locate fixture-specific requirements efficiently.

General regulations account for 5 items. These questions can require familiarity with broader plumbing-code provisions that apply across multiple systems. Candidates should avoid focusing only on the largest topics and should review the general requirements that influence installation and code compliance.

Interceptors and traps account for 4 items. Study trap requirements, trap seals, prohibited arrangements, interceptors, separators, and other related provisions. Understanding the purpose of these components can make code requirements easier to interpret.

The examination also contains regulatory questions covering standards of practice, standards of conduct, renewal and reinstatement, definitions, qualification for licensure, and revocation of licensure. These topics should be reviewed directly in the Virginia regulations.

Live virtual instruction can help candidates work through the examination content in an organized sequence. Rather than attempting to study every chapter at once, students can focus on one technical area at a time and then reinforce it through independent practice.

Self-study is especially valuable for code navigation. Candidates should repeatedly practice locating answers in the International Plumbing Code. The goal is to become familiar enough with the book that major topics, tables, chapters, and index terms are recognizable before the examination begins.

Practice questions can be used to strengthen both knowledge and navigation. Instead of checking an answer immediately, candidates should locate the supporting code provision whenever possible. This reinforces where information is found and helps build habits for open-book testing.

Time management should also be part of preparation. With 80 items and 210 minutes, candidates should avoid spending excessive time searching for a single difficult answer. Familiarity with the books and strong subject recognition can help create a more efficient testing approach.

The scope includes the installation, alteration, and repair of solar water-heating systems operating at temperatures not exceeding 220 degrees Fahrenheit. It includes thermosyphon systems, direct open-loop systems, and indirect closed-loop systems while excluding air as the heat-transfer medium.

Authorized work can include collectors, storage tanks, expansion tanks, heat exchangers, piping, valves, pumps, sensors, and low-voltage controls connected to existing plumbing and electrical stub-outs at the water-tank location.

The classification also includes solar heating systems for swimming pools when those systems connect to and operate from the conventional pool system. Non-solar plumbing, electrical, and mechanical systems and components remain outside the classification scope.

Backup and auxiliary heating systems may be included when they are part of the original contract and are integral to the solar collector or storage equipment. Contractors should remain within the exact authority granted by the classification.

The CR-78 trade examination contains 60 questions. Candidates are allowed 150 minutes and must earn a minimum passing score of 70 percent.

The examination content includes general plumbing, pipes and materials, open-loop and closed-loop systems, pumps and storage systems, system design, collectors, and controls. Questions may be based on the approved references, trade knowledge, or general industry practices.

General plumbing preparation may include water distribution, valves, pressure, temperature, fittings, piping arrangements, backflow considerations, system testing, drainage, supports, and code requirements that affect solar thermal installations.

Pipes and materials preparation may include copper, plastic, steel, insulation, fittings, joining methods, compatibility, temperature limitations, pressure ratings, thermal expansion, supports, corrosion, and protection from physical damage.

Open-loop system study may include potable water flowing directly through the solar collector, circulation methods, freeze vulnerability, scale formation, isolation, storage, and system controls. Candidates should understand the advantages and limitations of direct solar water-heating systems.

Closed-loop system study may include a separate heat-transfer fluid, heat exchangers, pumps, expansion control, pressure relief, air removal, freeze protection, fluid compatibility, and separation from the potable water system.

Pump and storage preparation may involve circulators, pump sizing, flow, head, storage tanks, expansion tanks, heat exchangers, valves, controls, and system sequencing. Candidates should understand how component selection affects circulation and heat delivery.

System-design preparation may include collector orientation, tilt, shading, storage capacity, piping layout, insulation, heat loss, pressure, freeze protection, stagnation, overheating, backup heat, maintenance access, and integration with existing plumbing systems.

Approved reference materials may be highlighted, underlined, annotated, and indexed before the exam session begins. The Arizona CR-37 Plumbing classification allows the scopes of work permitted by both the commercial C-37 Plumbing and residential R-37 Plumbing classifications. This dual classification is intended for contractors who perform plumbing work in both residential and commercial settings.

The plumbing scope includes installation, alteration, and repair of plumbing performed within property lines and not on public easements or rights-of-way, except as permitted by the classification. It includes piping, fixtures, and appliances related to water supply; pressure vessels and tanks; venting and sanitary drainage systems; septic tanks and leaching lines; roof leaders; lawn sprinklers; water conditioning equipment; and piping and equipment for swimming pools.

The scope also includes piping, fixtures, appliances, and pressure vessels for manufactured and natural gases, compressed air and vacuum systems, petroleum, fuel oil, non-potable liquids, hot water heating and hot water supply systems within listed pressure and temperature limitations, steam heating and steam supply systems within listed operating pressure limitations, gas or oil fired space heaters and furnaces excluding duct work, water cooling system piping excluding refrigerant piping and equipment, and testing and balancing of hydronic systems.

Sewer, gas, and water lines, and connections from a structure to the nearest point of public supply or disposal, may cross public or private easements or be installed within private easements under the scope limitations. Pipe installed across public property may not be increased in size or make another connection between the point of exit from private property and the point of connection at public supply or disposal. These lines may not be installed parallel to main lines in public easements or rights-of-way.

The Arizona Registrar of Contractors issues residential, commercial, and dual contractor licenses. The C-78 Solar Plumbing, Liquid Systems Only classification is the commercial specialty license for qualifying solar water-heating work using liquid as the heat-transfer medium.

The qualifying party is the individual whose experience, trade knowledge, and examination qualifications support the contractor license. This person must satisfy the applicable Arizona requirements and remain associated with the licensed business in the qualifying capacity recognized by the state.

C-78 preparation may include solar water heating, solar pool heating, thermosyphon systems, direct systems, indirect systems, collectors, storage tanks, expansion tanks, heat exchangers, pumps, valves, sensors, controls, piping, insulation, pressure relief, freeze protection, roof mounting, testing, maintenance, mathematics, and OSHA safety.

Direct open-loop systems circulate potable water through the solar collector. Candidates should understand the conditions that affect the suitability of these systems, including climate, water quality, freeze potential, stagnation, piping layout, controls, and protection of system components.

Indirect closed-loop systems use a separate heat-transfer fluid that circulates between the collectors and a heat exchanger. Preparation may include heat-transfer fluids, heat exchangers, expansion control, pumps, air elimination, pressure, fill procedures, flushing, freeze protection, and separation from the potable-water system.

Thermosyphon systems rely on natural circulation created by temperature and density differences. Candidates should understand the relationship between the collector and storage tank, pipe routing, flow resistance, system mounting, supports, and proper component placement.

Collector preparation may include flat-plate collectors, evacuated-tube collectors, absorber surfaces, glazing, headers, risers, insulation, enclosures, mounting hardware, orientation, tilt, spacing, shading, roof attachment, weather protection, and access for service.

Storage preparation may include solar storage tanks, auxiliary tanks, tank placement, insulation, connections, temperature control, pressure relief, thermal expansion, heat exchangers, stratification, and coordination with backup water-heating equipment.

Pump and control preparation may involve circulators, differential-temperature controllers, sensors, relays, switches, check valves, isolation valves, balancing valves, flow meters, and control sequences. Candidates should understand how controls start, stop, and protect a solar-thermal system.

Freeze-protection study may include drainback systems, antifreeze systems, recirculation methods, pipe drainage, insulation, control strategies, heat tracing, fluid concentration, and climate-related installation decisions.

Overheat and stagnation preparation may include pressure relief, expansion tanks, heat rejection, collector covers, control logic, fluid selection, system sizing, storage capacity, and procedures used when solar energy exceeds the available load.

Piping preparation may include approved materials, sizing, supports, insulation, expansion, valves, unions, drains, vents, penetrations, routing, slope, compatibility, corrosion protection, pressure testing, flushing, and identification.

Solar pool-heating preparation may involve collector arrays, pumps, filters, valves, bypass arrangements, check valves, sensors, controllers, roof mounting, piping layout, drainage, flow balancing, system startup, and seasonal shutdown.

Roof-mounted system preparation may include ladders, fall protection, attachment points, structural coordination, collector supports, roof penetrations, flashing, wind exposure, lifting, material handling, and safe access for installation and maintenance.

Trade mathematics may involve fractions, decimals, percentages, area, volume, flow, pressure, temperature difference, capacity, pipe length, offsets, heat transfer, collector area, storage volume, and unit conversion.

Trade mathematics should also receive dedicated review. Mathematics for Plumbers and Pipefitters, 8th Edition supports calculations involving measurements, areas, volumes, pipe dimensions, slopes, offsets, and other mathematical concepts used in plumbing and pipefitting work.

IPT’s Pipe Trades Handbook adds practical field information involving pipe materials, fittings, dimensions, formulas, terminology, and common pipe-trade data. This type of reference can be especially useful when studying practical construction and calculation concepts.

The package also includes references for boilers, hydronic heating, wastewater treatment, underground utilities, and construction safety, giving candidates a broad base for commercial plumbing preparation.

Open Book Test

The Arizona Plumbing Commercial Contractor (C-37) exam should be prepared for as an open book test. Open-book testing requires candidates to combine technical knowledge with efficient reference navigation.

Having the books available does not replace studying. The International Codes, NFPA standards, plumbing mathematics books, boiler references, hydronic-heating texts, and state regulatory materials contain substantial amounts of technical information. Candidates should become familiar with the books before exam day rather than relying on searching unfamiliar references under time pressure.

For plumbing-system questions, the International Plumbing Code should be one of the first references considered. Fuel-gas questions may point toward the International Fuel Gas Code, while mechanical-system questions may require the International Mechanical Code.

Fire-sprinkler questions require careful identification of the applicable standard. NFPA 13, NFPA 13D, and NFPA 13R address different system applications, so candidates should understand which reference is likely to contain the answer before beginning a search.

Wastewater subjects can be reviewed through the Arizona Administrative Code material included in the package. Safety questions can be studied through OSHA 29 CFR Part 1926, while underground utility awareness can be reinforced through the Arizona 811 - Arizona Blue Stake Brochure.

Mathematical questions can be studied with Mathematics for Plumbers and Pipefitters, while IPT’s Pipe Trades Handbook can support practical pipe data and trade-reference topics. Boiler and hydronic questions can be studied through Boiler Operator’s Guide and Modern Hydronic Heating for Residential and Light Commercial Buildings.

During practice sessions, identify the subject first, then select the reference most likely to contain the information. Use the table of contents, index, chapter headings, definitions, technical tables, and section organization to improve navigation speed.

Licensing Steps

Preparing for the C-37 trade examination is one part of pursuing an Arizona contractor license. Candidates should also keep the administrative, business, qualifying, and documentation requirements associated with contractor licensing organized.

  1. Determine the license applicant. Decide whether the contractor license will be pursued by an individual or through an eligible business entity.
  2. Select the appropriate contractor classification. Identify the commercial plumbing classification associated with the work the business intends to perform.
  3. Complete the contractor license application. Provide the legal applicant name, contact information, business details, and requested classification.
  4. Identify the qualifying individual. Make sure the person responsible for satisfying the trade qualification is properly associated with the applicant.
  5. Complete applicable examinations. The qualifying individual completes the required trade and business-related examinations associated with the licensing process.
  6. Provide required business documentation. Business entities should organize documentation applicable to their legal structure.
  7. Complete applicable bonding or financial requirements. Prepare the documentation required as part of the contractor licensing process.
  8. Submit remaining application materials. Complete outstanding documentation and correct any deficiencies identified during application review.

Candidates should coordinate exam preparation with the licensing process. Keeping study responsibilities and application requirements organized at the same time can help create a smoother path toward completing the contractor licensing process.

State Requirements

Arizona Plumbing Commercial Contractor candidates should prepare for both the technical examination and the administrative requirements associated with contractor licensing.

The legal applicant name should remain consistent throughout the licensing process. If an LLC, corporation, partnership, or other eligible business entity applies, the information submitted during licensing should correspond with the entity seeking the contractor license.

The licensing process can involve qualifying-party information, examination requirements, entity documentation, bonding, and other administrative items. Candidates should organize these responsibilities while studying for the C-37 trade exam.

Commercial plumbing work can also intersect with Arizona-specific requirements involving wastewater treatment and underground utilities. The included Arizona Administrative Code wastewater material and Arizona 811 information support preparation for those state-focused subjects.

Completing an exam book package does not itself issue a contractor license. Candidates must still complete the applicable Arizona contractor licensing requirements associated with the classification being pursued.

Study NFPA 13, NFPA 13D, and NFPA 13R together. The goal is not simply to recognize the book titles but to understand the application of each sprinkler standard and become familiar with where key system requirements are organized.

Use the Arizona Administrative Code material for wastewater-treatment topics and Arizona 811 for underground utility awareness. OSHA 29 CFR Part 1926 should remain part of the study rotation for construction safety.

This package combines the code books allowed in the examination with additional technical references intended for study before test day.

The package includes the Uniform Plumbing Code, 2018, NFPA 54 - Standard for National Fuel Gas Code, 2012, NFPA 58 - Standard for Liquid Petroleum Gas Code, 2014, and Uniform Mechanical Code, 2012 as exam-room references. It also includes Mathematics for Plumbers and Pipefitters, 8th edition, Code of Federal Regulations - 29 CFR Part 1926 (OSHA), Modern Hydronic Heating for Residential and Light Commercial Buildings, John Siegenthaler, P.E., 2022, Solar Water and Pool Heating Design and Installation Manual, Pipefitter's Handbook, and Pipe Welding Procedures, 2003 as study references that are not allowed into the trade examination.

The Nevada C-1D Plumbing Contractor exam is an open-book examination. Candidates should develop both plumbing trade knowledge and strong reference-navigation skills. Knowing which code book to use for a particular question can save valuable time when working through plumbing, gas, mechanical, venting, sizing, and installation problems.

The examination contains 80 questions, allows 3 hours for completion, and requires 56 correct answers to pass. The test covers a wide range of plumbing contractor knowledge, including water supply, drainage, waste and vent systems, gas systems, water heaters, hydronics, backflow, traps, cleanouts, plumbing mathematics, safety, solar systems, joints and connections, and storm drainage.

The Nevada C-1D classification itself is broad. It includes sanitary plumbing systems, water supply, waste and vent systems, roof drainage, landscape irrigation, hydronic heating systems not exceeding 200,000 BTUs, potable-water heating systems including solar equipment, gas supply systems, and piping for compressed air, vacuums, and medical gases. This package gives candidates references that support preparation across that wide scope.

What You Get

  • Uniform Plumbing Code, 2018 — exam-room reference for plumbing systems, fixtures, water supply, drainage, venting, backflow, traps, storm drainage, testing, and general plumbing requirements.
  • NFPA 54 - Standard for National Fuel Gas Code, 2012 — exam-room reference supporting fuel-gas piping, appliances, combustion air, venting, testing, and related gas-system requirements.
  • NFPA 58 - Standard for Liquid Petroleum Gas Code, 2014 — exam-room reference for LP-Gas piping, storage, regulators, containers, installation, and safety.
  • Uniform Mechanical Code, 2012 — exam-room reference supporting mechanical systems, hydronic applications, venting, equipment, and related mechanical requirements.
  • Mathematics for Plumbers and Pipefitters, 8th edition — study reference for calculations, measurements, pipefitting mathematics, and practical trade arithmetic.
  • Code of Federal Regulations - 29 CFR Part 1926 (OSHA) — study reference for construction safety.
  • Modern Hydronic Heating for Residential and Light Commercial Buildings, John Siegenthaler, P.E., 2022 — study material for hydronic heating systems, piping, controls, components, and design concepts.
  • Solar Water and Pool Heating Design and Installation Manual — study reference for solar water-heating applications and installation principles.
  • Pipefitter's Handbook — practical piping, fitting, measurement, layout, and field-reference material.
  • Pipe Welding Procedures, 2003 — study material covering pipe welding methods, joint preparation, techniques, and workmanship.

Exam Details

The Nevada C-1D Plumbing Contractor examination contains 80 questions. Candidates receive 3 hours to complete the examination and must answer 56 questions correctly to pass.

The examination content is divided into the following areas:

  • Gas Systems: 8 questions
  • Cleanouts: 4 questions
  • Fixtures and Equipment: 3 questions
  • Hydronics: 3 questions
  • Water Heaters/Venting: 6 questions
  • Piping, Valves, and Controls: 5 questions
  • Water Supply: 8 questions
  • Hangers and Supports: 4 questions
  • Drain, Waste, and Vents: 8 questions
  • Backflow: 4 questions
  • Traps and Interceptors: 4 questions
  • Isometric Analysis/Plumbing Mathematics: 6 questions
  • Safety: 5 questions
  • Joints and Connections: 3 questions
  • Solar: 3 questions
  • General Plumbing Requirements: 3 questions
  • Storm Drainage: 3 questions

Gas Systems, Water Supply, and Drain, Waste, and Vents are among the largest categories, with eight questions each. Candidates should be comfortable navigating applicable code provisions while understanding the practical installation principles behind each system.

Plumbing mathematics is also important. The exam includes six questions involving isometric analysis and plumbing calculations, so candidates should practice solving trade problems rather than depending solely on code lookups.

Open Book Test

The Nevada C-1D Plumbing Contractor examination is an open-book test.

The following references in this package are allowed into the examination:

  • Uniform Plumbing Code, 2018
  • NFPA 54 - Standard for National Fuel Gas Code, 2012
  • NFPA 58 - Standard for Liquid Petroleum Gas Code, 2014
  • Uniform Mechanical Code, 2012

The other books included in this package are study references and are not allowed into the examination.

With 80 questions in three hours, candidates should not plan to search multiple books for every answer. Effective open-book preparation means learning the subject first and then knowing which reference is most likely to contain the applicable requirement.

For example, drainage, water supply, fixtures, cleanouts, traps, backflow, and storm drainage questions will often involve the Uniform Plumbing Code. Fuel-gas questions may require NFPA 54, while LP-Gas topics may lead to NFPA 58. Mechanical or hydronic questions may involve the Uniform Mechanical Code.

Practice should include timed reference navigation. Candidates can select a subject, identify the appropriate book, locate the applicable section or table, and repeat the exercise until the process becomes more efficient.

Licensing Steps

  1. Confirm the C-1D classification. Make sure Nevada Plumbing Contractor licensing matches the work the business intends to perform.
  2. Identify the qualifying individual. The contractor application must identify the person providing the required experience and trade qualification.
  3. Document qualifying experience. The qualifying individual must meet Nevada's applicable experience requirements for the requested classification.
  4. Submit the contractor license application. Complete the required application and supporting documentation with the Nevada State Contractors Board.
  5. Receive examination eligibility. After the application and qualifications are accepted, proceed with examination scheduling.
  6. Prepare for the C-1D trade examination. Study plumbing systems, gas systems, hydronics, solar, calculations, safety, and code navigation.
  7. Prepare for Contractor Management Survey requirements. Nevada contractor licensing includes the applicable business and law examination requirement unless an authorized waiver applies.
  8. Complete the required examinations. Take the applicable trade and business examinations.
  9. Complete remaining licensing requirements. Finish the additional requirements associated with issuance of the Nevada contractor license.

State Requirements

Nevada's C-1D Plumbing classification authorizes installation and maintenance of material and fixtures used to provide sanitary conditions in buildings through a permanent supply of safe water and sanitary waste and vent systems required for proper waste removal.

The classification also includes roof drainage systems, landscape irrigation systems, systems used to heat potable water including solar equipment, and hydronic heating systems not exceeding 200,000 British thermal units.

C-1D work includes a permanent means of supplying gas for residential and industrial purposes, along with piping for compressed air, vacuums, and gases used for medical purposes. The classification also permits applicable water and gas piping between the edge of a building and the utility meter.

For contractor qualification, Nevada generally requires the qualifying individual to have at least four full years of experience at the journeyman, foreman, supervisor, or contractor level within the applicable period before filing the application.

The breadth of the C-1D scope explains why the examination covers plumbing code, fuel gas, LP-Gas, hydronic systems, solar water heating, mathematics, safety, water distribution, drainage, venting, and storm systems.

    This study-only reference supports construction safety preparation involving tools, excavation, ladders, personal protective equipment, electrical hazards, material handling, and general jobsite safety.
  • Modern Hydronic Heating for Residential and Light Commercial Buildings, John Siegenthaler, P.E., 2022
    This study reference supports preparation involving hydronic heating principles, piping arrangements, circulators, heat emitters, controls, system components, and practical hydronic design concepts.

  • NFPA 58 - Standard for Liquid Petroleum Gas Code, 2014
    Approved for use during the examination for applicable LP-Gas requirements.
  • Uniform Mechanical Code, 2012
    Approved for use during the examination for applicable mechanical and hydronic-system requirements.

Test Information and Study Materials

A productive C-1D preparation plan should start with the major plumbing systems. Water Supply study should include sizing, pressure, materials, valves, backflow prevention, distribution, supports, and system protection. Candidates should practice locating applicable tables and requirements in the Uniform Plumbing Code.

Drain, Waste, and Vent Systems should include drainage sizing, slope, vents, fixture units, cleanouts, connections, traps, interceptors, and general sanitary drainage requirements. Practice interpreting both written questions and plumbing diagrams.

Gas Systems should be studied with NFPA 54 and NFPA 58 nearby. Learn the difference between natural gas and LP-Gas systems and practice identifying which reference should be used for a particular question.

Water Heaters and Venting should include appliance installation, venting, temperature and pressure protection, combustion air, clearances, and fuel-gas considerations.

Hydronics should include basic hot-water heating principles, circulators, piping arrangements, controls, heat emitters, expansion, and system operation. The Modern Hydronic Heating reference provides additional study support for this subject.

Plumbing Mathematics and Isometric Analysis should be practiced repeatedly. Work through pipe sizing, elevations, measurements, areas, volumes, offsets, and other calculations until the process can be completed efficiently.

Safety should be studied before test day because OSHA is not allowed into the examination. Candidates should develop enough familiarity with construction safety principles to answer these questions from retained knowledge.

Solar preparation should include the major components and basic operating principles of solar water-heating systems. The solar design and installation manual can help strengthen this portion of the exam.

Code navigation should be part of every study session. Rather than reading all four allowed books from beginning to end, candidates should practice finding answers to targeted questions and learn where major subjects are located.

A useful exercise is to sort practice questions by reference. Create separate groups for UPC, NFPA 54, NFPA 58, and UMC questions. This helps build the habit of choosing the correct book before beginning the lookup.

Timed practice is also important. Three hours for 80 questions gives candidates a little over two minutes per question on average. Candidates should learn when to perform a code lookup and when to answer from trade knowledge and move forward.

  9. Complete the required examinations. Take the applicable trade and business examinations.
  10. Complete remaining licensing requirements. Finish the additional requirements associated with issuance of the Nevada contractor license.

State Requirements

Nevada's C-1 Plumbing and Heating Contracting classification is a broad specialty license. A person holding the primary C-1 classification may perform work authorized under the C-1 subclassifications.

The scope includes boilers and hot-water or steam piping with related fittings, valves, gauges, pumps, radiators, tanks, fuel-oil lines, chimneys, flues, and associated work. It also includes fire sprinkler systems and insulation of pipes and ducts.

C-1 work also extends to plumbing systems providing safe water, sanitary waste and venting, roof drainage, hydronic heating systems within the applicable classification scope, landscape irrigation, potable-water heating systems including solar equipment, and gas supply systems.

The classification further reaches into sheet metal fabrication and installation, heating and evaporative cooling systems, gas pipes and vents, water heaters, chilled-water piping, firefighter breathing-air systems, and industrial piping used to transport water, steam, gas, chemicals, food, and other substances.

Because the primary C-1 classification covers such a wide range of work, the examination is considerably broader than a plumbing-only test. Candidates should prepare for both plumbing and mechanical construction along with specialized subjects such as fire sprinklers, industrial piping, hydronics, refrigeration-related systems, welding, and safety.

Test Information and Study Materials

A productive Nevada C-1 study plan should divide preparation into major systems rather than attempting to read every reference from beginning to end.

Drain, Waste, and Vent Systems should receive substantial attention. Review drainage sizing, slope, vents, fixture units, cleanouts, traps, interceptors, and sanitary-system requirements using the Uniform Plumbing Code.

Water Supply preparation should include sizing, pressure, materials, valves, backflow protection, supports, distribution, and system protection. Candidates should practice locating applicable UPC tables quickly.

Gas Systems should be studied with NFPA 54 and NFPA 58. Learn how natural gas and LP-Gas systems differ and practice selecting the correct reference before beginning a lookup.

Fire Sprinklers should be studied with NFPA 13. Focus on sprinkler systems, piping, components, spacing concepts, and installation requirements relevant to the C-1 examination.

Hydronics and Boilers should include heating-system components, pumps, valves, piping, heat transfer, controls, and boiler-related knowledge. The UMC and Modern Hydronic Heating reference can be used together during preparation.

Chilled Water Piping accounts for 6 questions. Candidates should review piping materials, valves, pumps, supports, insulation considerations, and system-operation concepts associated with chilled-water distribution.

Plumbing Mathematics and Isometric Analysis accounts for 8 questions. Practice pipe calculations, dimensions, elevations, geometry, offsets, areas, volumes, and plan interpretation until the steps become familiar.

Industrial Piping should include system materials, valves, equipment, supports, joining methods, and piping used for water, steam, gas, chemicals, food, and other industrial substances.

Safety should be learned before test day because the OSHA reference is not allowed into the examination. Use the study reference to strengthen knowledge of jobsite hazards, protective equipment, tools, excavation, and general construction safety.

Welding knowledge can support industrial and mechanical piping preparation. Review joint preparation, welding methods, equipment, workmanship, and safe procedures using Modern Welding.

Heating, Cooling, and Refrigeration concepts should also be part of the study plan because the C-1 classification includes heating and air-circulation work. Modern Refrigeration and Air Conditioning can support this broader mechanical review.

Reference navigation should be practiced under timed conditions. Choose a question, identify whether it belongs in the UPC, UMC, NFPA 13, NFPA 54, or NFPA 58, and then locate the applicable provision. The ability to choose the correct book quickly can save as much time as knowing how to use the index.

  • Project Management and Supervision: 7 questions
  • Contracts: 5 questions
  • Financial: 8 questions

  1. Gain qualifying plumbing trade experience. Oklahoma contractor applicants must meet the experience requirements established for plumbing licensing.
  2. Meet the plumbing journeyman qualifications. Contractor applicants must satisfy the same basic qualification requirements applicable to an Oklahoma plumbing journeyman.
  3. Complete additional contractor-level experience. Applicants must obtain an additional year of qualifying plumbing trade experience beyond the journeyman-level requirement.
  4. Apply for the plumbing contractor license. Plumbing contractor licensing is administered through the Oklahoma Construction Industries Board.
  5. Receive approval for examination. Candidates must be approved before proceeding with the required contractor examinations.

Approved plumbing education can substitute for a portion of the required trade experience. Qualifying education must meet the standards established for plumbing licensing in Oklahoma.

Contractor applicants are required to pass both portions of the contractor examination: the applicable plumbing trade examination and the Plumbing Business and Law examination.

After the required examinations are completed, the contractor license remains inactive until the applicable bond and insurance requirements are satisfied.

An active Oklahoma plumbing contractor is required to maintain a $5,000 corporate surety bond or another qualifying form of security permitted under Oklahoma plumbing regulations.

Active plumbing contractors must also maintain at least $50,000 in commercial general liability insurance. Maintaining required coverage is part of keeping a plumbing contractor license active.

Licensed plumbing contractors also have continuing responsibilities involving apprentice supervision, licensing, advertising, contracts, bids, insurance, and compliance with Oklahoma plumbing laws and regulations.

Exam Details

The Oklahoma Plumbing Contractor and Natural Gas examination evaluates knowledge associated with plumbing installation, water supply, sanitary drainage, vents, piping materials, fixtures, fuel gas systems, and construction safety.

The Oklahoma Construction Industries Board administers plumbing contractor licensing, and PSI delivers the examination.

  • Exam Name: Oklahoma Plumbing Contractor and Natural Gas
  • Licensing Authority: Oklahoma Construction Industries Board
  • Testing Provider: PSI
  • Number of Scored Questions: 85
  • Time Allowed: 180 minutes
  • Passing Score: 75%
  • Minimum Correct Answers: 64
  • Exam Format: Open book

The technical examination includes ten principal subject areas:

  • General Plumbing Knowledge and Regulations: 10 questions
  • Piping, Valves, and Control Valves: 8 questions
  • Fixtures and Equipment: 8 questions
  • Water Supply: 10 questions
  • Drains and Sewers: 10 questions
  • Vents: 13 questions
  • Traps, Interceptors, Indirect, and Special Waste: 5 questions

  • Fuel Gas: 10 questions

Venting represents the largest individual examination category, with 13 questions. General plumbing knowledge, water supply, drains and sewers, and fuel gas are also heavily represented.

Plumbing and natural gas contracting in Oklahoma is regulated by the Oklahoma Construction Industries Board under the state's plumbing licensing laws and administrative regulations.

Plumbing contractors perform work involving water supply systems, sanitary drainage, plumbing fixtures, venting, piping installations, and other regulated plumbing activities. Natural gas piping work also requires familiarity with fuel gas materials, sizing methods, regulators, testing, and installation requirements.

The Oklahoma Uniform Building Code Commission adopts statewide construction codes, including the International Plumbing Code and International Fuel Gas Code, with applicable Oklahoma amendments.

  2. Meet journeyman-level qualifications. Contractor applicants must meet the qualification requirements applicable to an Oklahoma plumbing journeyman.
  3. Complete additional contractor experience. Oklahoma requires an additional year of qualifying plumbing trade experience for contractor-level licensing.

State Requirements

Oklahoma plumbing contractor licensing is administered by the Oklahoma Construction Industries Board. Applicants for a plumbing contractor license must meet the qualification requirements applicable to a plumbing journeyman and complete an additional one year of experience in the plumbing trade.

The standard journeyman pathway includes applicants who are at least 18 years old and have three years of qualifying plumbing trade experience while employed by a licensed plumbing contractor. Oklahoma also recognizes qualifying alternatives provided under its licensing requirements.

Approved plumbing education may substitute for a portion of the required experience when the education meets Oklahoma requirements. Contractor applicants must still satisfy the additional contractor-level experience requirement.

Once the applicable examinations have been completed, additional requirements apply before the contractor license is active. An active Oklahoma plumbing contractor generally must maintain the required contractor bond and commercial general liability insurance.

The Oklahoma Construction Industries Board requires an active plumbing contractor to maintain a $5,000 corporate surety bond, subject to the alternatives and requirements established under Oklahoma plumbing regulations.

An active plumbing contractor must also provide evidence of at least $50,000 in commercial general liability insurance. Maintaining required coverage is an ongoing responsibility associated with active contractor status.

Oklahoma plumbing contractors are also responsible for complying with applicable requirements involving apprentice supervision, license display, advertising, contracts, bids, continuing education, and other obligations established by Oklahoma plumbing law and regulations.

The Electrical Contractors Licensing Law, Board rules, and NASCLA business reference are included for closed-book preparation. Candidates should review these books thoroughly before the examination because licensing and business questions must be answered without consulting them during the test.

Permanent tabs may be used when they comply with current testing requirements. Temporary tabs, removable notes, divider tabs, loose sheets, attached papers, and unauthorized inserts are not allowed.

Open-book testing requires familiarity with the NEC. Candidates should practice using the index, table of contents, definitions, article structure, tables, exceptions, and cross-references so they can locate information efficiently.

A question involving an air conditioning unit may require the equipment nameplate provisions and the NEC article covering air conditioning and refrigeration equipment. A question involving a pump motor may require the general motor provisions and applicable motor tables.

  3. Confirm the business relationship. The applicant must be primarily engaged in or regularly employed by a lawful plumbing, heating, or air conditioning business in North Carolina and prepared to serve as its listed qualified individual.

The North Carolina State Board of Examiners of Electrical Contractors regulates the SP-PH examination and license. The Board establishes applicant qualifications, reviews experience, authorizes examinations, issues licenses, and enforces the Electrical Contractors Licensing Law and related rules.

An applicant for the Special Restricted Plumbing and Heating classification must document at least 3,000 hours of qualifying experience. At least 2,000 hours must be primary experience. The remaining hours may consist of primary experience, secondary experience, or a combination of both.

Applicants may receive credit for qualifying service gained in the plumbing, heating, or air conditioning field when the experience falls within categories recognized by the Board. Experience must be documented according to the examination application requirements.

The applicant must verify that the applicant is primarily engaged in or regularly employed by a lawful plumbing, heating, or air conditioning business in North Carolina and will serve as the listed qualified individual for that business.

The SP-PH license authorizes installation, maintenance, or repair of electrical wiring or devices only as an incident to the license holder’s plumbing, heating, or air conditioning business.

The authorized wiring must be directly related to plumbing, heating, or air conditioning equipment. It is limited to circuits or portions of circuits operating at no more than 600 volts phase to phase.

Exam Details

The North Carolina Plumbing Technician examination allows four hours. It is a technical examination focused on plumbing work, code compliance, safety, and the responsibilities associated with the technician qualification.

The examination may address water supply and distribution, sanitary drainage, venting, plumbing fixtures, water heaters, indirect waste, special waste, storm drainage, traps, interceptors, separators, fuel gas systems, residential plumbing, permits, inspections, and licensing laws.

Water-supply preparation should include approved materials, water-service installation, pipe sizing, pressure requirements, valves, fixture supplies, backflow protection, cross-connection control, thermal expansion, protection from freezing, and prevention of contamination.

Drainage study may involve drainage fixture units, horizontal and vertical pipe sizing, minimum slopes, changes in direction, cleanouts, building drains, building sewers, stacks, branch piping, sumps, ejectors, and connections to approved disposal systems.

Venting preparation should address trap-seal protection, individual vents, common vents, wet venting, circuit venting, stack venting, vent stacks, relief vents, air admittance valves, developed length, pipe sizing, and termination requirements.

Fixture questions may involve water closets, lavatories, sinks, bathtubs, showers, laundry fixtures, floor drains, drinking fountains, service sinks, fixture supports, clearances, accessibility, drainage connections, and minimum fixture requirements.

Water-heater subjects may include approved locations, temperature and pressure relief protection, discharge piping, drain pans, shutoff valves, thermal expansion, combustion considerations, venting, clearances, and installation requirements.

Fuel gas preparation may include approved pipe and tubing materials, pipe sizing, pressure limitations, regulators, shutoff valves, appliance connectors, testing, combustion air, chimneys, venting systems, equipment installation, and protection of piping from damage.

Residential plumbing questions may require candidates to identify requirements that apply specifically to one- and two-family dwellings and townhouses. Candidates should understand when the Residential Code controls and how its plumbing provisions relate to the general Plumbing Code and Fuel Gas Code.

Administrative and licensing questions may address permits, inspections, construction documents, approvals, code-official authority, technician supervision, license responsibilities, prohibited conduct, and enforcement procedures.

Open Book Test

The North Carolina Plumbing Technician examination is an open-book test. Candidates must bring the approved references assigned to the examination and ensure that each book meets the current testing requirements.

The North Carolina Administrative Code and Policies, Plumbing Code, Fuel Gas Code, Residential Code, and Board’s Laws & Rules are identified for Plumbing Technician examinations. Candidates should prepare with these same editions so the chapter organization, section numbers, tables, definitions, and indexes are familiar before test day.

Original hard-bound, spiral-bound, or ring-bound editions are permitted when they remain in their published condition. Approved loose-leaf codebooks must remain in the original binders supplied by the publisher.

Commercially available, permanently attached index tabs may be used. Highlighting is permitted. Written notes, formulas, calculations, underlining, homemade tabs, unauthorized divider pages, loose sheets, taped inserts, and printed PDF copies are not allowed.

Candidates should inspect every book before the examination. Unauthorized markings or added material may prevent a reference from being accepted at the testing center.

Open-book testing still requires thorough preparation. The four-hour testing period does not provide enough time to read unfamiliar chapters from the beginning. Candidates should practice identifying the subject, selecting the correct reference, locating the governing section, and confirming the answer efficiently.

A sanitary drainage question should direct the candidate to the Plumbing Code. A gas-pipe sizing question belongs in the Fuel Gas Code. A residential water-heater question may require the Residential Code, while a permit or inspection question may require the Administrative Code and Policies.

Questions involving licensing authority, supervision, professional conduct, or technician responsibilities should direct the candidate to the Board’s Laws & Rules. Knowing which book controls each topic can reduce unnecessary searching during the examination.

Practice should include the table of contents, index, definitions, chapter headings, tables, figures, appendices, and cross-references in every book. Candidates should read the complete provision because exceptions, limitations, or related sections may affect the correct answer.

Licensing Steps

  1. Select the plumbing technician qualification. Review the available Plumbing Technician Class I and Class II qualifications and choose the category that matches the applicant’s experience and intended work.
  2. Obtain the required reference books. Applicants should have the approved books before submitting the examination application and should be ready to test using those references.
  3. Document qualifying experience. Collect records showing hands-on experience in plumbing installation, maintenance, service, or repair.
  4. Complete the technician application. Provide the requested personal information, employment history, qualification category, and licensing information.
  5. Obtain the required criminal background report. Follow the Board’s current instructions and include the required report with the application.
  6. Submit employer verification forms. Each applicable employer must verify the qualifying plumbing experience using the required forms.
  7. Provide employment records. Include the supporting wage, tax, or employment documentation requested by the Board.
  8. Submit the completed application and examination fee. Ensure that all forms are complete, signed, notarized when required, and supported by the necessary records.
  9. Receive examination approval. The Board must review and approve the application, background report, and experience documentation before the applicant may test.
  10. Schedule the examination. Approved applicants receive instructions for scheduling the computer-based examination with the Board’s testing provider.
  11. Prepare the exam books. Confirm that all references comply with the current rules for binding, commercial tabs, highlighting, and markings.
  12. Complete the Plumbing Technician examination. Follow all testing-center rules involving identification, security, reference materials, and examination conduct.
  13. Complete license issuance requirements. Passing the examination satisfies the testing component, but the applicant must complete all remaining Board requirements before the technician license is issued.

State Requirements

The North Carolina State Board of Examiners of Plumbing, Heating and Fire Sprinkler Contractors regulates Plumbing Technician licensing. The Board evaluates applicants, verifies experience, authorizes examinations, issues licenses, and enforces the laws and rules governing licensed plumbing work.

An applicant for a Plumbing Technician examination must document 3,000 hours of qualifying experience in the installation, maintenance, service, or repair of plumbing systems. The experience must be relevant to the technician qualification requested.

Approved trade education may provide up to 50 percent credit toward the experience requirement. Eligible education must be directly related to the trade and completed through a college, university, community college, or technical institute as part of an applicable certificate or diploma program.

The application must include experience-verification forms completed by the appropriate employers or licensees. Supporting employment records, such as the documentation requested in the application packet, must also be submitted.

Applicants must obtain the nationwide criminal background report required by the Board. The completed application, background report, experience records, and required fees must be received and approved before the applicant is authorized to sit for the examination.

A Plumbing Technician qualification is different from a Plumbing Contractor license. A technician credential does not independently authorize the holder to advertise, bid, contract, or operate a plumbing contracting business.

Technicians perform work within the employment and supervision structure permitted by North Carolina law and Board rules. The licensed contractor or qualifying license holder remains responsible for contracts, permits, supervision, and work performed under the contractor license.

The Board’s technician application includes Plumbing Technician Class I and Plumbing Technician Class II qualifications. Applicants should select the category that matches the type of plumbing experience they can document and the scope under which they will work.

A person who already holds the equivalent contractor license issued by the Board and seeks the corresponding technician license may qualify for an examination exemption under the Board’s current procedures.

License holders must keep their personal and employment information current and comply with renewal requirements. Changes in the technician’s employment or association with a license holder should be handled according to the Board’s applicable rules and forms.

  • International Plumbing Code, 2021

Test Information and Study Materials

Start your preparation with drain, waste, vent, and sewer systems because this is the largest subject area on the examination. Review drainage-system design, fixture units, pipe sizing, venting, cleanouts, slopes, materials, connections, and related requirements. Practice finding the applicable provisions in the International Plumbing Code rather than relying only on memorization.

General plumbing knowledge and regulations are also heavily represented. Candidates should understand terminology, system requirements, materials, installations, code principles, and practical plumbing practices. Definitions are especially important because plumbing-code questions often depend on the precise meaning of a technical term.

Isometric analysis accounts for nine questions on the current exam. Candidates should practice interpreting plumbing drawings and recognizing how fixtures, branches, stacks, vents, drains, and piping systems relate to one another. Isometric questions may require both visualization skills and knowledge of plumbing-code requirements.

Piping, valves, and controls should receive dedicated review. Become familiar with common piping materials, permitted uses, fittings, joints, valves, supports, connections, and installation practices. Understanding why a particular material or valve is used can help with both direct trade questions and code-based questions.

Water supply preparation should include water distribution, pipe sizing concepts, pressure, fixtures, connections, and protection of the potable water system. Backflow protection and cross-connection concepts are important areas for plumbing contractors to understand.

Fixtures and equipment should be studied together with applicable code requirements. Review installation, clearances, connections, fixture requirements, water heaters, and equipment-related provisions that may apply to residential plumbing systems.

Fuel gas represents a dedicated portion of the examination. Study gas piping, materials, sizing concepts, appliance connections, combustion air, venting, shutoff requirements, and related installation principles. LP gas and fuel oil also appear separately on the examination outline and should not be overlooked.

OSHA safety is another tested subject. Plumbing contractors frequently work around excavations, trenches, ladders, power tools, electrical equipment, elevated work areas, and active construction sites. Become familiar with the organization of 29 CFR Part 1926 so safety information can be located efficiently.

Use the highlighted books actively throughout preparation. When reviewing highlighted material, read the surrounding provisions and identify related tables, exceptions, definitions, and cross-referenced sections. Understanding the context of a code rule is more useful than remembering a highlighted sentence in isolation.

Timed practice can help candidates develop an effective examination rhythm. With 80 questions and four hours available, candidates have an average of three minutes per question. Some trade-knowledge questions may be answered quickly, while isometric or code-research questions may require additional time.

Because MSBOC establishes examination eligibility, application preparation should begin alongside technical study. Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Mississippi Residential Plumbing classification?

The Residential Plumbing classification covers installation, maintenance, and repair of residential plumbing systems. The holder of the classification is limited to residential plumbing work.

How many questions are on the Mississippi Residential Plumbing exam?

The current examination contains 80 questions. Candidates receive four hours and must achieve at least 70 percent to pass.

Is the Mississippi Residential Plumbing exam open book?

Yes. The examination is open book, and candidates may bring approved references into the PSI testing center under examination rules.

What is the largest subject area on the exam?

Drain, waste, vent, and sewer systems represent the largest individual area with 17 questions. General plumbing knowledge and regulations account for another 15 questions.

Are the books in this package highlighted?

Yes. This product is the Highlighted Edition, designed to support organized study and faster recognition of selected material.

What books are included in this package?

The package includes 29 CFR Part 1926 OSHA, International Plumbing Code 2021, International Fuel Gas Code 2021, and International Residential Code 2021.

Can highlighted references be used on the PSI exam?

Yes. PSI permits approved references to be highlighted, underlined, and indexed before the examination. Permanent tabs are allowed, while temporary removable tabs are prohibited.

Can I use a calculator during the exam?

Yes. PSI permits a silent, nonprinting, non-programmable calculator for the Residential Plumbing examination.

Why should I practice isometric analysis?

Isometric analysis accounts for nine questions on the current examination. Candidates should be comfortable interpreting piping layouts and understanding relationships among fixtures, drains, vents, and piping systems.

Does Mississippi require an exam for Residential Plumbing?

Yes. The Mississippi State Board of Contractors identifies Residential Plumbing as a classification requiring a trade examination.

How does the Application Accelerator help?

The Application Accelerator provides application-focused support designed to help candidates organize the licensing process while preparing for the Residential Plumbing examination.

Does this package guarantee that I will pass or receive a license?

No. Exam results depend on the candidate's preparation and performance, while license approval depends on meeting Mississippi State Board of Contractors requirements. The package is designed to support an organized preparation process.

What books are included in the Virginia Residential Plumber Tradesman Book Package?

How many questions are on the Residential Plumber exam?
