Open-book does not eliminate the need to know the trade—it increases the value of being able to confirm details fast and avoid costly second-guessing.

Open Book Test

This package is designed for an open book testing environment where code lookups are part of the exam strategy. In Georgia, the journeyman reference materials may be used during the examination, while the bulletin notes that reference materials may not be used for the other plumbing exams.

The most effective open-book strategy is built around three skills:

  • Recognition: identify what the question is really asking (definitions, sizing, materials, installation requirements, prohibited practices, or exceptions).
  • Location: quickly determine where that topic lives in the code (chapter, section, table, or the index).
  • Confirmation: verify the requirement in the exact code language, including any exceptions, footnotes, or related provisions.

The IPC is dense by design. Using it well is a learned skill. Tabs support the “location” step by helping you jump to the right chapter area faster, but the real advantage comes from consistent practice with the code until navigation becomes second nature.

Licensing Steps

Journeyman Plumber licensing is handled through the state licensing process and exam administration procedures. In Georgia, the plumbing licensure examinations are administered through PSI and require an application/approval process before scheduling.

  1. Confirm the license path: Ensure you are applying for Journeyman Plumber (not Master Plumber Class I or Class II).
  2. Submit your application: Follow the Georgia application process for the Journeyman Plumber examination.
  3. Receive approval to test: Once approved, you’ll receive scheduling instructions through the exam administrator.
  4. Schedule and sit for the exam: Complete both exam parts within the allotted time.
  5. Complete remaining licensing requirements: Follow the Board’s instructions for any post-exam licensing steps once you pass.

A practical approach is to start studying early, build your code navigation habits, and schedule your test when you can consistently answer timed practice sets without getting stuck in the book.

State Requirements

Georgia’s plumbing licensure is overseen by the Georgia Construction Industry Licensing Board through the Division of Master and Journeyman Plumbers. The PSI candidate bulletin describes the Division’s role in establishing minimum standards and requiring passage of licensure examinations as part of entry into the profession. The bulletin also notes that exam appointments are administered by PSI at test centers located throughout Georgia and at select locations in nearby states.

Georgia’s exam framework includes three license classifications: Journeyman Plumber, Master Plumber Class I (Restricted), and Master Plumber Class II (Unrestricted). This package is positioned specifically for journeyman-level exam preparation under IPC-based standards.

Important for Georgia candidates planning ahead: the suggested reference list and bulletin language indicate the exam is tied to Georgia code editions and amendment sets, and the reference list notes that, beginning May 1, 2026, the exam is based on the 2024 Georgia Plumbing Code (2024 International Plumbing Code with Georgia amendments).

Reference Books

  • 2021 International Plumbing Code
    The IPC is the central reference for plumbing code questions, including general regulations, fixtures, water supply and distribution, sanitary drainage, vents, and specialized systems. It’s the book you’ll use to practice reading requirements precisely and confirming correct installation standards.
  • Journeyman Plumber Exam Study Guide (Softbound)
    A structured companion resource that reinforces code comprehension and journeyman-level plumbing topics through focused review and practice. Use it to strengthen your approach to interpreting code language, applying requirements to scenarios, and building consistent test-day habits.

Test Information and Study Materials

Your study is most effective when you combine “know it” learning with “find it” practice. Journeyman plumbing exams are built around real-world plumbing knowledge and code-based decision-making, which means you’ll typically face questions that test your ability to:

  • Interpret code requirements correctly: understand what is required, what is permitted, and what is prohibited.
  • Navigate drainage and venting rules: trap and vent concepts, drainage system fundamentals, and code-driven installation requirements.
  • Work through water supply topics: distribution concepts, fixture supply expectations, and code-driven provisions that impact installation.
  • Apply fixture and installation standards: practical compliance choices that match the intent of the code.
  • Use definitions and exceptions effectively: many questions hinge on a definition, a key term, or an exception that changes how a rule applies.

To build speed for an open-book environment, practice with a simple routine:

  • Daily navigation drills (10–20 minutes): choose a topic and locate 10 related code sections using the index and table of contents, then summarize the rule in one sentence.
  • Timed practice sets (2–3 times per week): simulate real pressure by setting a timer and forcing yourself to make clean, confident code lookups.
  • Weak-area rotation: focus on the chapters where you lose time—then repeat them until your search process speeds up.
  • Question-to-code mapping: after each practice set, write down which IPC chapter/section answered each question. This builds your mental “map” of the book.

The included Quick Reference Tabs for the 2021 IPC support this routine by improving physical navigation while you practice. That matters most when you’re under time pressure and need to move directly to the correct chapter area without flipping through dozens of pages.

How 1 Exam Prep Helps You Reach Your Goal

1 Exam Prep supports journeyman plumber candidates by keeping preparation structured, practical, and trade-focused. Instead of bouncing between scattered resources, you get a clear foundation: the IPC as your primary reference, tabs to support efficient navigation, and a study guide that reinforces how to interpret and apply code requirements.

  • Organized study guidance: Build a repeatable plan that keeps you moving through high-value code areas instead of getting lost in the details.
  • Trade-focused review: Strengthen the plumbing knowledge behind the code so questions feel familiar and easier to interpret.
  • Practice-oriented preparation: Develop consistent exam habits—careful reading, clean lookups, and confident answer selection.
  • Reference navigation support: Open-book exams reward candidates who can find answers quickly and confirm details accurately. Tabs and repeated code practice help build that speed.
  • Confidence-building structure: When your process is consistent—identify the topic, locate the section, confirm the rule—you reduce hesitation and improve performance under pressure.

The goal is to help you prepare the right way: understand the code, practice using it efficiently, and walk into the exam with a system you can rely on.

FAQ

Is the Journeyman Plumber exam open book in Georgia?

Yes. Georgia’s journeyman plumber exam allows the listed reference materials to be used during the examination, per the PSI candidate information bulletin.

What’s included in this exam prep package?

This package includes the 2021 International Plumbing Code, Quick Reference Tabs for the 2021 IPC, and a Journeyman Plumber Exam Study Guide (softbound book).

How long is the Georgia Journeyman Plumber exam?

The Georgia Journeyman exam allows a total of 5 hours and is administered in two parts: 2.5 hours for Part 1, a break, then 2.5 hours for Part 2.

How many questions are on the Georgia Journeyman Plumber exam?

The PSI bulletin lists 100 scored test questions plus 20 pretest questions, for a total of 120 questions presented during the exam session.

What score do I need to pass?

Georgia uses scaled scoring for the plumbing exams, and a final scaled score of 70 is required to pass.

Do the Quick Reference Tabs replace studying the code?

No. Tabs make navigation faster, but they work best when you practice with the code consistently. The combination of understanding the rule and finding it quickly is what improves performance in an open-book format.

What’s the best way to use the IPC during study?

Use the index, table of contents, and chapter structure every time you practice. Train yourself to identify the topic first, then locate the section and confirm the requirement—including exceptions and definitions.

Is this package only for Georgia?

This package is built for journeyman plumber candidates preparing under IPC-based standards. Always match your exam’s required code edition to the code book you study from.

Exam Details

Closed Book Test

The Georgia Master Plumber Class I (Restricted) examination is a closed-book test. Candidates cannot consult plumbing codes, technical manuals, reference books, or personal study notes during the examination.

This examination format places particular importance on understanding and remembering plumbing principles. Candidates must recognize technical problems, interpret practical scenarios, and apply code-related knowledge without searching for answers in a reference book.

For example, a drainage question may involve applying pipe sizing principles or understanding proper venting arrangements. A fuel gas question may involve identifying safe installation practices, appliance connections, or combustion air requirements.

Questions involving plumbing mathematics may require measurements, conversions, slope calculations, or other technical operations. Professional responsibility questions may address contractor management, workplace safety, and applicable regulations.

State Requirements

Georgia Master Plumber Class I licensing is regulated by the State Construction Industry Licensing Board, Division of Master and Journeyman Plumbers.

Qualifying Experience: Under Georgia's licensing requirements effective July 1, 2026, Master Plumber Class I applicants must complete a minimum of four years of qualifying full-time plumbing experience.

Licensed Journeyman Experience: At least three of those years must be completed while licensed as a Journeyman Plumber. Applicants who obtained their Journeyman Plumber license before March 1, 2025, are covered by a transitional provision requiring at least one year of licensed journeyman experience within the four-year total.

Licensed Supervision: Qualifying experience must be obtained under the supervision of a licensed Master Plumber and must relate to plumbing work within the Class I scope.

Relevant Plumbing Work: Experience may involve installation, maintenance, alteration, service, repair, system layout, pipe sizing, material selection, inspections, testing, and troubleshooting.

Experience Verification: Applicants must provide signed affidavits from licensed Master Plumbers who supervised or oversaw their qualifying work.

Application Requirements: Applicants must complete the prescribed licensing application and submit the required identity, experience, and supporting documentation.

Examination Requirement: Candidates must pass the Board-approved Master Plumber Class I examination with a minimum score of 70.

Restricted License Scope: Georgia Master Plumber Class I licensing covers plumbing involving single-family dwellings, one-level dwellings designed for no more than two families, and commercial structures not exceeding 10,000 square feet in area.

Class II Distinction: Master Plumber Class II is the unrestricted classification. Professionals intending to undertake plumbing contracting beyond the Class I scope require the appropriate authorization.

Is the Georgia Journeyman Plumber Exam open book?

Yes. Candidates may use authorized reference publications during the examination according to PSI and Georgia licensing Board requirements.

How many scored questions are on the examination?

The Journeyman Plumber examination content outline includes 100 scored questions covering general laws, regulations, plumbing methods, and practical trade knowledge.

What passing score is required?

Georgia requires a minimum score of 70 on the Board-approved Journeyman Plumber examination.

What plumbing topics should I study?

Important areas include water distribution, drainage, venting, plumbing fixtures, fuel gas systems, plumbing mathematics, pipe installation, accessibility, excavation safety, and applicable regulations.

The course supports preparation involving plumbing and fuel gas code knowledge. The associated study references include the 2024 International Plumbing Code, 2024 International Fuel Gas Code, and Georgia amendments.

How much plumbing experience is required in Georgia?

Georgia's licensing requirements effective July 1, 2026, establish at least one year of qualifying full-time plumbing experience under the supervision of an appropriately licensed Master Plumber.

Does a Journeyman Plumber license authorize me to operate a plumbing business?

No. Georgia distinguishes Journeyman Plumber licensing from Master Plumber licensing. Operating a plumbing contracting business requires the appropriate Master Plumber license.

Can I use highlighted and tabbed reference books during the examination?

Authorized reference materials may be highlighted and tabbed under Georgia's examination rules. Books containing handwritten notes or comments are not permitted.

The course is designed for plumbing apprentices, experienced plumbing technicians, and qualified trade professionals preparing for Georgia Journeyman Plumber licensing.

Does completing the course guarantee a plumbing license?

No. Applicants must meet Georgia's experience and application requirements, pass the approved examination, and complete the licensing process.

Exam Details

The exam is designed to measure the minimum knowledge needed to perform residential plumbing work for the public in a competent and responsible manner.

Students should prepare for questions related to plumbing fixtures, water supply and distribution, sanitary drainage, venting, traps, cleanouts, materials, piping methods, equipment, testing, code definitions, safety, and related residential plumbing installation topics.

Open Book Test

Applicants should follow the Commission’s instructions for application forms, supporting documentation, experience affidavits, fees, and exam eligibility requirements.

The standard examination path includes the Residential Plumbing technical exam and the Business Management and Law for Residential Builders exam. The technical exam measures residential plumbing trade knowledge. The exact examination outline, scheduling procedures, approved references, testing rules, and candidate requirements may depend on the examination pathway used for South Carolina contractor qualification. The International Plumbing Code is generally the primary reference for plumbing-system requirements. The International Fuel Gas Code supports questions involving fuel gas piping and connected equipment. The mathematics book helps candidates review the calculations needed to solve trade problems, while the South Carolina 811 Excavator Manual provides guidance for excavation and underground utility safety.

South Carolina regulates commercial plumbing work through the South Carolina Contractor’s Licensing Board. Plumbing is listed as a mechanical contractor classification. Businesses and individuals performing regulated commercial construction must obtain the appropriate license when the work meets the state’s licensing threshold and falls within a regulated classification.

  1. Identify the correct classification. Confirm that the Plumbing mechanical contractor classification matches the work the business intends to offer and perform.

  3. Complete the required examinations. Applicants qualifying by examination must pass the applicable technical examination. South Carolina also requires qualifying-party applicants to satisfy the state Business Management and Law examination requirement for commercial contractors.
  4. Document qualifying experience. Examination applicants are generally required to provide proof of at least two years of full-time experience completed within the preceding five years in the classification being requested. The experience should primarily reflect commercial work.
  5. Submit the qualifying-party application. After completing the applicable examination requirements, submit the required qualifying-party certification application and supporting documentation to the South Carolina Contractor’s Licensing Board.
  6. Submit the contractor license application. The business must complete the appropriate General and Mechanical Contractor application and provide the required company, financial, qualifying-party, and organizational information.
  7. Meet financial or bonding requirements. Contractor group limitations are connected to financial documentation or surety-bond requirements. Applicants should select the group that matches their intended project limits and submit the required supporting material.
  8. Receive approval before contracting. Passing an examination alone does not create a contractor license. The applicant must complete the Board’s certification and licensing process before offering or performing work that requires licensure.

Application forms, documentation requirements, and licensing procedures can change. Candidates should use the current forms published by the South Carolina Contractor’s Licensing Board when applying.

State Requirements

The South Carolina Contractor’s Licensing Board regulates general and mechanical contractors performing commercial construction. The Plumbing classification falls within the mechanical contractor category. A properly licensed contractor must have a qualified individual associated with the license for the requested classification.

South Carolina requires applicants using the examination route to complete the appropriate technical examination and the Business Management and Law examination for commercial contractors. The technical examination addresses the trade classification, while the business examination covers the administrative and legal knowledge involved in operating a contracting business.

Applicants must also demonstrate the required experience for the classification. The Board’s current qualifying-party instructions call for at least two years of full-time work experience performed within the previous five years for applicants qualifying through the examination process. Experience documentation should describe the work performed and show that it is relevant to the Plumbing classification.

The business license application and the individual qualifying-party certification are related but separate parts of the process. The qualifying party demonstrates technical qualification, while the contractor business must satisfy the Board’s organizational, financial, and application requirements.

South Carolina contractor licenses include group limitations that determine the maximum value of work the contractor may undertake under the license. The requested group affects the financial statement, working-capital, net-worth, or surety-bond documentation that may be required. Applicants should review the current application instructions carefully before selecting a group.

Commercial and residential plumbing licensing should not be treated as interchangeable. The South Carolina Contractor’s Licensing Board regulates commercial general and mechanical contracting, while residential licensing matters may fall under the South Carolina Residential Builders Commission. Candidates should pursue the license category that corresponds to the type of construction they intend to perform.

Reference Books

  • International Plumbing Code, 2021 Edition
    This code provides requirements for plumbing-system design and installation. Major subject areas include plumbing fixtures, water-supply and distribution systems, sanitary drainage, venting, traps, interceptors, storm drainage, special piping, and related code administration. Candidates should become familiar with the definitions, tables, chapter structure, and methods used to locate system requirements.
  • International Fuel Gas Code, 2021 Edition
    This reference addresses fuel gas systems and gas-fired equipment. It includes provisions related to fuel gas piping, pipe sizing, system testing, appliance installation, combustion air, venting, chimneys, clearances, and safety. Candidates should practice using the index and tables to locate requirements efficiently.
  • Mathematics for Plumbers and Pipefitters, Lee Smith, 8th Edition, 2013
    This trade mathematics book supports the numerical side of plumbing and pipefitting work. It helps candidates review measurements, fractions, decimals, percentages, geometry, formulas, pipe-related calculations, offsets, elevations, and practical problem-solving methods used in the field.
  • South Carolina 811 Excavator Manual
    This manual explains responsibilities associated with excavation near underground utilities. It supports study of notification procedures, utility-locate markings, tolerance zones, safe digging practices, damage prevention, and appropriate actions when underground facilities are exposed or damaged.

Test Information and Study Materials

A strong study plan should combine code reading, reference-navigation practice, calculation review, and timed question work. Reading the books from beginning to end is rarely the most efficient approach. Begin by learning what each reference covers, then organize study sessions around the major knowledge areas relevant to commercial plumbing.

For the International Plumbing Code, focus on understanding how the code is structured. Review definitions before studying technical chapters because code questions often depend on the precise meaning of a term. Become comfortable locating requirements for fixtures, water distribution, sanitary drainage, venting, traps, cleanouts, indirect waste, storm drainage, and system testing.

For the International Fuel Gas Code, study the relationship between piping requirements, appliance installation, combustion air, and venting. Practice locating sizing tables and reading the notes that accompany them. Tables often contain conditions or limitations that affect the correct answer.

Use Mathematics for Plumbers and Pipefitters to identify calculation areas that need additional practice. Work problems without immediately checking the solution. Write down each step, label units, and confirm that the final answer is reasonable. Candidates should be comfortable converting measurements and applying formulas under time constraints.

Review the South Carolina 811 Excavator Manual as a practical safety document. Pay attention to the sequence of actions expected before excavation begins, the meaning of locate markings, responsibilities while digging, and procedures to follow when a facility is damaged or disturbed.

During practice sessions, set a time limit and use the books exactly as you plan to use them during the examination. When an answer is incorrect, do more than record the correct choice. Locate the controlling code section or explanation and determine why the other choices were wrong.

Read the full question, identify the subject, select the correct reference, locate the controlling information, complete any required calculation, and compare the result with the available answer choices. The International Plumbing Code, 2021 Edition, is the primary technical code used with this course. It addresses plumbing fixtures, water-distribution systems, sanitary drainage, venting, traps, interceptors, piping materials, joints, testing, inspections, storm drainage, and related installation requirements.

Water-distribution preparation may involve service piping, distribution piping, pipe sizing, water demand, pressure, materials, valves, backflow protection, joints, supports, testing, and fixture supply. Candidates should learn how to locate applicable tables and understand how the code organizes general and system-specific requirements.

Sanitary-drainage preparation may involve fixture units, horizontal branches, stacks, building drains, building sewers, cleanouts, slopes, pipe sizing, materials, joints, supports, and testing. Questions may require direct code lookup, interpretation of a table, or application of practical plumbing knowledge.

Venting subjects may include vent sizing, developed length, vent connections, wet venting, common venting, circuit venting, stack venting, vent terminals, and prohibited arrangements. Candidates should understand how vent systems protect trap seals and support proper drainage-system performance.

Fixture-related preparation may include required fixture quantities, installation, clearances, supports, water-supply connections, drainage connections, accessibility considerations, materials, and testing. Additional subjects may involve traps, interceptors, separators, indirect waste, special plumbing systems, and storm drainage.

The Code of Federal Regulations, 29 CFR Part 1926, supports preparation involving federal construction-safety requirements. Plumbing professionals may need to review excavation, trench protection, ladders, scaffolds, fall protection, personal protective equipment, tools, equipment, electrical hazards, and material handling.

Plumbing work can involve trenches, heavy piping, elevated work areas, temporary power, lifting equipment, confined spaces, and interaction with other trades. Candidates should connect written safety requirements with the practical hazards encountered on construction projects.

Mathematics for Plumbers and Pipefitters, 8th Edition, supports preparation involving measurements, fractions, decimals, percentages, ratios, geometry, areas, volumes, pressures, pipe calculations, offsets, and unit conversions.

The “2012 International Plumbing Code (IPC)” establishes minimum regulations for plumbing systems through prescriptive and performance-related provisions, covering areas such as fixtures, water supply and distribution, sanitary drainage, venting, storm-drainage systems, traps, interceptors and fuel-gas piping, and it serves as one of the core code references used in various contractor licensing exams supported by 1 Exam Prep. As an ICC-published standard, the 2012 IPC provides uniform technical requirements for design, installation and inspection of plumbing systems, making it a key open-book resource for exam topics involving code compliance, system sizing, materials, accessibility requirements and field application methodologies.


The 2012 IPC provides minimum regulations for plumbing facilities in terms of both performance and prescriptive objectives, and provides for the acceptance of new and innovative products, materials, and systems. Important changes to the IPC include: Requirements for the design of a Siphonic Roof Drainage System have been added. Gray water recycling requirements have moved to the body of the code in a new Chapter 13. “Hydro-mechanical” and “Gravity” are the new terms for the two general types of grease interceptors. Air admittance valves complying with standard ASSE 1049 are now allowed for venting chemical waste systems. The length of a combination waste and vent system is now unlimited. The Single Stack Vent System method has been added. The code expands on suitable materials for pressurized sewage discharge applications and ratings. The IPC also includes its companion document, 2012 International Private Sewage Disposal Code®, that contains provisions for design, installation, and inspection of private sewage disposal systems, and provides flexibility in the development of safe and sanitary systems. The authorized scope includes sanitary drainage, storm drainage, venting, public and private water supply systems, septic tanks, drainage and supply wells, swimming pool piping, irrigation, and solar water heating systems.

Florida Plumbing Contractors may also perform specified work involving water, natural gas, liquefied petroleum gas, medical gas systems, pressure piping, and other specialized systems within their authorized classification.

Contractors must comply with applicable construction codes, approved plans, specifications, safety requirements, and professional regulations.

  2. Apply through the state’s licensing process: Submit the correct application for your classification and meet any documentation requirements listed by the Board.
  3. Receive exam eligibility/authorization: Once approved, follow the exam scheduling instructions provided for your division.
  4. Schedule and pass the required examination(s): Prepare with the correct references and study materials listed for your trade exam.
  5. Complete any remaining licensing steps: After passing, follow Board instructions to finalize licensing.

State Requirements

Requirements can differ by division and license class under the Georgia Construction Industry Licensing Board. Confirm your current requirements directly through the Georgia Professional Licensing Boards Division and your specific trade division’s application checklist so you submit the correct forms and supporting documents.

FAQ

Who is this 5th Edition Georgia NASCLA guide for?

This edition is labeled for Georgia Construction Industry Licensing Board candidates, including Plumbers, Conditioned Air, Low Voltage, Electrical, and Utility Contractors.

Is this book allowed in the exam room?

Some Georgia Construction Industry Licensing Board exams allow approved references during testing. Always confirm permitted references using the current candidate handbook/bulletin for your exact division and exam.

Is this an open-book exam?

Open-book vs. closed-book rules depend on the specific Georgia trade exam and the current published candidate handbook. If your bulletin includes an approved reference list for use during the examination, follow those rules exactly.

Can I highlight or tab the book?

If your exam allows this book as a reference, the testing rules for that exam will specify what markings and tabs are permitted. Follow the current exam rules for your division to ensure your book is compliant on test day.

Does this include a course or only the book?

This product is the reference book. If you want an online prep course or a tabs bundle option, choose the matching course or bundle listing.
